oneOf.description: 8x8 tiles (the asset map format `chr-2bpp`).
Palettes (`palette`).
Metatiles with their properties (`metatiles`).
A grid of metatile numbers (`level-grid`).
Rows of numbers (`table`).

Lists of objects that build a level's tiles, one list per entry
(`smb-area-objects`, `smb2-level-objects`, or Mega Man 2's
`mm2-screens`).

Lists of objects that place entities in a level, one list per entry
(`smb-enemy-objects`, `smb2-enemy-objects`, or `mm2-spawns`).
Rows of bytes, such as a game's sprite frames (`byte-rows`).

A text encoding: which tile stands for each character, read from
the `charset` of a text asset (`ppu-strings`). Presentation only.

Tiles written to places on the screen, as a console's update
strings write them (`ppu-strings`): a status bar's fixed text.
Presentation only.

Sprite frames as layouts of tiles, each tile with its own place in
pixels, flips, palette and tiles slot, with the sprite palettes
each level showed (`sprite-set`, written by `gp sprites capture`
from a game's sprite tables and recordings; docs/formats/sprite-set.md).
Presentation only. Since core 0.4.2.

Songs as notes per channel, with their patterns, instruments and
tempo in frames (`gp-songs`, written by `gp sound capture` from a
recording's APU register log or by `gp sound decode` from a known
driver's data; docs/formats/songs.md). Presentation only. Since
core 0.4.3.

Sound effects in the same form, each tied to the model event it
marks. Presentation only. Since core 0.4.3.

AssetSlot.description: A named place for an asset. The model refers to assets only by slot.

capture.description:
For a `songs` or `sound-effects` slot: the capture that fills it,
a recording's frames read by `gp sound capture`. Like `from`, a
recipe: the songs are game content and stay outside the repo.
Since core 0.4.3.

entities.description:
For a `spawn-objects` slot: the entity type each object kind number
places, by entity name. An object whose number isn't listed places
nothing in the model.

from.description:
The lifting recipe that fills the slot: an asset of an asset map
(assets/<source>.toml). A commercial-game template ships the slot
empty with only this recipe.

item_roles.description:
A role for each item in the asset, in order (each metatile of a
tileset, each palette of a palettes slot), for themes and the
readability check. Required for metatiles and palettes slots from
core 0.3.1 on.

role.description: What the asset is for (docs/model.md lists the roles).

tiles.description:
For a `screen-text` slot: the `tiles` slot its layouts are drawn
with where a screen shows them (`present.screens`), in place of
the level's (feature `assets.screen_tiles`): a screen the game
draws with another pattern table or CHR bank. Donkey Kong: Original
Edition draws its title with CHR bank 1 (the hook at $C8F3).
For a `level-objects` slot filled from update strings: the `tiles`
slot a level drawn from it uses, in place of the level's (feature
`assets.layout_tiles`); Original Edition draws 50m with CHR bank 1
($CB5D -> $838A). Presentation only.

every.description: Frames shown, then as many hidden.

Bounce.description:
Since 0.4.10: after it moves, the tile at `point` (from its position)
is looked at. A tile there that isn't empty, water or a ladder, met
while moving down for the first frame in a row, bounces it: its speed
up and down becomes `speed`, its fraction kept (FireballBGCollision
stores $fd in Fireball_Y_Speed and leaves the force alone), and its
whole height is rounded down to a
multiple of `snap`, its fraction kept. One met while moving up, or on
the frame after a bounce, removes it. Super Mario Bros.' fireballs
(FireballBGCollision, BlockBufferChk_FBall): a wall is met the same way,
so a fireball dies against one. Above `from_y` nothing is looked at.

BumpPresent.description:
A held cell's bump: how it moves, where its picture is, and the
picture by the kind it will have, as a game draws the bouncing block
as sprites.

offset.description: The picture's top left in pixels from the cell's.

sprites.description:
By the tile kind the cell will have: the bump's picture, tiles
from a `tiles` slot as a sprite's (`slot`, `tiles`, `width`,
`palette`, `cells`). A kind without one draws the cell's metatile
with its backdrop clear.

oneOf.description: An arcade coin slot.
An arcade one-player start button.
An arcade player's first button (Tapper's tap).

ByMove.description:
A camera that moves forward (right or down) by the followed entity's
whole-pixel move this frame, by where the entity was in the view on the
frame before, in whole pixels from the view's top left corner: not at
all while that place is under `from`, the move less `short_by` (but at
least a pixel) from `from`, and the whole move from `full` on. A move
back or none doesn't move it. Super Mario Bros.' ScrollHandler is 80,
112 and 1.

from.description: The place in the view, in pixels, where it starts to move.

full.description: The place where it moves by the whole move.

hold_with_counters.description:
Since core 0.4.23: `push_hold` is a frame timer: it counts down on
every frame the `counters` system runs (not frozen, not stopped by a
state), whether a state stops the camera or not, and on no other.
Super Mario Bros.' DecTimers counts SideCollisionTimer down at the
start of each frame unless TimerControl is set, and ScrollLock, which
stops ScrollHandler, doesn't stop it.

keep_move.description:
Since core 0.4.12: on a frame when a state stops the followed
entity's system (`stops`) and not the camera's, the camera moves as
if the entity had moved by its last move again. Super Mario Bros.'
ScrollHandler reads Player_X_Scroll, which only the player's
movement routines set, so the screen goes on scrolling while Mario
shrinks. The last move is world state (`cameras.<name>.move`).

push_hold.description:
Since core 0.4.11: after the followed entity is pushed out of a
wall (a platformer `run.walls` point or `jump.land_depth`), the
camera doesn't move on this many frames less one, from the next.
Super Mario Bros.' ImpedePlayerMove sets SideCollisionTimer to $10,
which ScrollHandler waits for, and DecTimers counts it down at the
start of each frame. The frames left are world state
(`cameras.<name>.hold`).

short_by.description: How much less than the move it moves between `from` and `full`.

by_move.description:
Moves by the followed entity's move instead of keeping it `lead`
from the corner; `lead` places it when a level starts. Since core
0.4.4.

clamp_to_level.description: Keeps the view inside the level.

follow.description: The entity type it follows (the first one spawned).

keep_in_view.description:
Since core 0.4.12: the followed entity's whole-pixel place in the
view across stays from the first to the second, checked each frame
after the camera's step, whether the camera moves or not. Past
either, the entity is put back at it, keeping the fraction of its
place, and its speed's whole steps across become 0 unless only the
direction away from that edge is held (its `run` actions). Super
Mario Bros.' ScrollHandler ends in ChkPOffscr and KeepOnscr: 0 and
239, the screen's right edge less 16.

keep_in_view_rows.description:
Feature `camera.keep_in_view_rows`: other bounds for `keep_in_view`
while the followed entity's row is in a range: its whole y on the
ground, and in the air the height it took off from when
`jump.fatal_drop` keeps it (mechanic word 3), else its y. The first
row that holds gives the bounds. Donkey Kong's edge test $D990 also
stops a walk left on 25m's sixth girder ($59 = 6) at sprite x 104,
short of Kong.

keep_in_view_touch.description:
Since core 0.4.17: `keep_in_view`'s first bound acts when the place
reaches it, not only past it, so an entity at that edge loses its
speed as one past it does. Super Mario Bros.' GetXOffscreenBits
sets bit 7 from a difference of 0, while the right edge's test
starts a pixel past its bound.

keep_in_view_turn.description:
Feature `camera.keep_in_view_turn`: an entity in the air at either
bound (or past it) moving toward it turns around, its speed across
reversed, instead of losing its speed there. Donkey Kong's jump
($D547) flips Mario's way ($56) at the screen's edge ($D990).

lead.description:
How far the followed entity's position is kept from the view's top
left corner, on each axis it moves along.

scroll_back.description: Can move back left (or up). Super Mario Bros.' camera can't.

size.description: Width and height of the view in pixels.

Carry.description:
Lifting, carrying and throwing `carryable` entities. `action` pressed
while standing on one lifts it: for `lift_frames` frames the carrier
doesn't move, then the entity rides at `offset` from the carrier's
position. `action` pressed again throws it: it takes `throw` (x
mirrored when facing left), or `throw_moving` when the carrier's speed
across is `moving_above` or more. `item.lifted` and `item.thrown` fire,
each concerning the item and the carrier.

offset.description:
Its offset from the carrier instead of the carry's, such as a
taller item's.

Cell.description: One tile of a sprite's layout. Presentation only.

at.description:
Where the tile goes, as a column and row of 8-pixel tiles from the
picture's top left, instead of its place in the rows of `width`.

palette.description: A palette for this tile instead of the sprite's.

CellsPresent.description:
How the cells the game changes are drawn (the feature `present.cells`). Presentation
only: the simulation changes the cells' kinds, and this says which
picture each new kind shows.

bump.description:
While a head hit holds a cell, the picture it will show (or its
own, when it stays as it was) rises and falls.

held.description: The metatile a cell shows while a head hit holds it.

kinds.description:
By tile kind (`empty`, `solid`, ...): the metatile a cell changed
to that kind is drawn with, by its number in the level's tileset
(a grid level's `metatiles` slot, or a layout's metatile sets).

Change.description:
One way a counter changes: when an event fires, or every so many
frames. Exactly one of `on` and `every`.

after.description:
Since core 0.4.13, with `on`: the change is made this many frames
after the event, counted every frame, frozen or not, from the next
one. Super Mario Bros. adds an enemy's points when its floatey
number's timer, set to $30 by SetupFloateyNumber, reads $2b in
FloateyNumbersRoutine, 5 frames after the kill. Default 0, at once.

every.description:
Frames between changes, counted in the `counters` system while
nothing freezes the world (or always, with the counter's
`runs_when_frozen`).

if.description:
Feature `change.if`, with `on`: the event changes the counter only
while this counter condition holds, tested as the event fires.
Donkey Kong's points routine ($D008) adds nothing while the attract
demo plays ($58), though the points sprite still shows.

of.description:
Since core 0.4.13, with `on`: only an event that concerns an entity
of one of these kinds changes it. Default any.

Climb.description:
Climbing ladders: tiles of kind `ladder`. `up` held with the hitbox's
middle on a ladder, or `down` held standing on a ladder's top, starts a
climb: the entity moves to the ladder's middle across and has no
gravity, moving `speed` a frame while `up` or `down` is held. It stops
climbing when its middle leaves the ladder, when it lands, or when
`release` is pressed.

by_feet.description:
Feature `climb.by_feet`: the ladder that holds the climber is the
row of pixels under its tile hitbox, not its middle. It climbs while
that row is in a ladder or a cell with a surface, stops where it
isn't (a broken ladder's top), and stands once it reaches a surface
row. Down starts a climb from a surface with a ladder under it.

down_cycle.description: Feature `climb.down_cycle`: the same for climbing down.

down_holds.description:
Feature `climb.down_holds`: `down` held while standing and not
climbing keeps the body still: the run gets no input and the step
counter doesn't step. Up held walks as usual (Donkey Kong's walk
routine looks for a ladder down instead of walking). A jump comes
first: the takeoff frame and a landing hold aren't held.

down_through.description:
Feature `climb.down_through`, with `by_feet`: down newly pressed
also starts a climb from standing with the feet in a ladder cell (a
ladder's foot), and climbing down tests nothing on the way: it goes on until
the feet reach a surface row, and the height wraps at this many
pixels, as an 8-bit coordinate does. Neither `kill_below` nor a
goal touches a body climbing so. Donkey Kong looks for a girder
only of the floor its y + 8 is in, and Down at a ladder's foot
climbs down through the floor, round the screen and onto the top
girder.

down_through_step.description:
Feature `climb.down_through_step`, with `down_through`: the press of
down at a ladder's foot climbs down through the floor only while the
entity's last move across stepped it up a surface. Donkey Kong's
walk tests the ground ($D20B) after the move across and before the
step up, so $5A is 0 after a step up the slope, and $D432 skips its
ladder-top test then (the ladder-zip, TASVideos 2299S).

grab.description:
Feature `climb.grab`, `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` from the entity's place, in
whole pixels: in a level with `ladders`, a climb up starts only
where this box (edges included) meets one of the level's ladder
boxes below the box's top row, instead of by the cell at the
entity's middle. Standing on a ladder's top, up does nothing (the
game's climb routine finds the top in a list of its own, $D50A).
Donkey Kong's ladder routine ($D28B) tests Mario's feet box against
each ladder's box ($D8AD).

grab_down.description:
Pixels it moves down into the ladder when it starts climbing down
from the top.

grab_snap.description:
With `grab` (feature `climb.grab`): a climb up by a ladder box
starts with the entity's x at the box's left plus this, instead of
the middle of the cell. Donkey Kong's $D2B9 puts Mario's sprite at
the ladder's x less 4 ($A1).

hold_still.description:
Holding this action keeps it still on the ladder (firing, in Mega
Man 2).

lone_way.description:
Feature `climb.lone_way`: the climb reads one way from the pad, as
the walk does with `run.lone_direction`: up or down starts or moves
a climb only held alone, and on a ladder left or right held alone
(both, with `run.both_left`) turns the climber to it without moving
it. Donkey Kong's $D175 latches $56 only for a lone direction and
writes $57 from Left or Right on every frame but a jump's or a
fall's, the ladder's too, and the ladder routine ($D37E) climbs on
$56 = 8 or 4 (wallW's ladder probes, 2026-11-04: Left on a ladder
faces left on the frame it is pressed; Down and Left stand still).

release.description: The action that lets go. Default none.

stand_on_top.description:
A ladder cell with no ladder above it stands like a `top` tile for
this entity while it isn't climbing.

top_test.description:
Feature `climb.top_test`, with `grab`: a climb from standing asks
the level's `ladder_tops` and `ladder_stops` by the grab box (edges
included). Down starts only where the box meets one of the level's
ladder boxes, and a top and no stop, at the ladder's left plus
`grab_snap`; up doesn't start where it meets a top or a stop; and
climbing, up doesn't move where it meets a stop. With
`down_through_step`, a press of down after a step up skips the top
and stop test but still needs the ladder box. Donkey Kong's ladder routine
asks $D50A on the girder while $5A is set ($D397 up, $D43B down)
and before each move ($D3AF, $D45A): 1 in a top's box, 2 in a
stop's.

up_cycle.description:
Feature `climb.up_cycle`: whole pixels moved up on each count of
the body's step counter (its mechanic word 0, shared with
`run.step_cycle`), in place of `speed`. A frame up is held at a
ladder steps the counter, and the climb starts on a count that
moves (Donkey Kong's $88 pattern at $D9E8, $24 and $49).

Clip.description:
A run of frames a sprite shows while its `when` holds. Presentation
only: it reads the entity's state and never changes it.

by_speed.description:
Frames each picture shows for, by the entity's speed: the first
step whose `at_least` its speed reaches (a step without one always
does). The time is picked again each time the picture changes, so a
faster entity steps faster.

clock.description:
What counts the time: `own` (the default), a timer per entity that
starts when the clip does; `game`, the frames the game has run,
so every entity showing the clip changes picture together; or
(since core 0.4.9) `body`, one timer per entity that runs down
whatever clip shows, as a game keeps one animation timer per
object: the clip steps after drawing a picture when the timer has
run out, and sets it again.

every.description:
Frames each picture shows for. Give this or `by_speed`; with
neither, a clip of one frame.

frames.description: The frames, shown in turn and then from the first again.

hold.description:
Never changes picture: it keeps the picture the entity showed when
the clip started, when that is one of its frames, and else shows
its first. A walk cycle that stops in the air is a held clip of the
walk's frames. Since core 0.4.2.

speed_before.description:
`by_speed` reads the speed the entity had on the frame before, as
a game that picks its animation's time before it moves. Super Mario
Bros.' GetPlayerAnimSpeed runs before ImposeFriction. Since core
0.4.18.

when.description: What must hold for the clip to show. Empty: always.

while_frozen.description:
Keeps changing pictures while the world is frozen. Without it the
clip stops while a `freeze` state holds the world.

ClipFrame.description:
One frame of a clip: a row of the sprite's `frame` slot or tile
numbers, or else the sprite's own frame, with flips and a layout.

cells.description:
Its tiles' flips, palettes and places, as the sprite's `cells`;
without them, the sprite's.

colors.description:
Its colors, as the sprite's `colors`, for a game that writes a
sprite palette while something lasts (Donkey Kong's 100m turns the
fires' palette blue from a hammer's touch to its end, $D89A and
$D7F2). Without it, the sprite's. Feature `clip.frame_colors`.

every.description:
Frames this picture shows for, in place of the clip's `every`, for
a game that holds some pictures longer than others (Donkey Kong's
Pauline calls for help in eight 16-frame steps, then waits). Every
frame of the clip gives one, or none does. Feature
`clip.frame_every`.

flip_x.description: The whole picture mirrored left to right, on top of any facing flip.

flip_y.description: The whole picture mirrored top to bottom.

offset.description:
Its picture's top left from the entity's position, as the sprite's
`offset`, for a game that places each picture of a turn apart
(Super Mario Bros.' hammer, DrawHammer). Without it, the sprite's.
Since core 0.4.21.

row.description: A row of the slot the sprite's `frame` names, or of `slot`.

slot.description:
The `rows` slot `row` is read from, in place of the sprite's frame
slot, for a game that keeps its pictures in tables of their own
(Donkey Kong's poses, each behind a size byte). Feature
`clip.frame_slot`.

tiles.description: Tile numbers, row by row, in the sprite's `width`.

oneOf.description: Since core 0.4.9.

ColorCycle.description:
A palette color that steps through a list over time, as a game's
palette rotation does.

colors.description: A `table` slot whose first column lists the colors in turn.

counter.description:
Since core 0.4.7: a counter whose value picks the color instead of
the frame count, for a game that keeps its color rotation's place in
a variable (a mapping can then carry the place into a clip's start).
The cycle's own `every` is then ignored. Give the counter a `max`
of the list's length less one, `wrap`, and an `every` change.

shift.description:
With `counter`: added to its value (modulo the list's length) to
find the color shown, for a game whose counter has already stepped
past the color on screen (-1). Default 0.

Contact.description: What happens when the player touches this entity.

after_move.description:
The touch is tested in the entity's own turn, after its move, not
before the enemies move. Super Mario Bros.' BulletBillHandler moves a
cannon's bill and then calls PlayerEnemyCollision, in ProcessCannons
after the enemy loop, so all the enemies have moved on the frame a
bill hits Mario. Default off.

bounce.description: The player's vertical speed after a stomp.

damage.description:
How much a `hurt-player` touch takes from the player's `health`.
Default 1.

every.description:
Since 0.4.9: the touch is tested only on frames whose number is a
multiple of this (the frame count from power-on), as Super Mario
Bros.' PlayerEnemyCollision leaves on frames whose FrameCounter is
odd. Default every frame.

in_turn.description:
Since 0.4.25: a state's `stops_at_once` that this touch sets off
leaves the bodies in earlier numbered slots to finish their move.
Super Mario Bros.' RunNormalEnemies tests a touch inside the enemy
loop, so TimerControl stops the enemy that hurt Mario and those after
it, and those before it have moved. Default off, and a body without a
numbered slot stops them all.

invincible.description:
Since 0.4.10: what a touch does while the player is invincible
(its `invincible`). Default `defeat` for an entity whose touch would
hurt or kill the player or kick it, or that can be stomped, and
`otherwise` for the rest. Super Mario Bros.' firebars and hammers
do nothing to a player with the star.

keep_on_stomp.description:
A stomp leaves the entity in place, for its state machine to change
(a Koopa into its shell, a Goomba flattened for a while).

near.description:
The touch is tested by the player's `touch_points` near the entity's
position, in the entity's turn after it moves, in place of the
hitboxes in the contact system. Super Mario Bros.' FirebarCollision
runs inside ProcFirebar. Default off.

phase.description:
Since 0.4.9, with `every`: the frames tested are those whose number
less this is a multiple of `every` (PlayerHammerCollision runs on
odd frames: `every = 2`, `phase = 1`). Default 0.

ride.description:
Since 0.4.26, with `stand`: how the player rides the entity. The player is placed
on the entity after the entity's own move on the same frame, keeping
the fraction of its height, as Super Mario Bros.' MoveSmallPlatform
and ChkYPCollision run PositionPlayerOnVPlat after the platform moves.
It needs `platformer.contact` before `platformer.enemies` in the
system order. Default off: the player is placed in the contact
system, on a whole pixel.

sides.description:
Since 0.4.22: the entity's sides stop the player. A touch at a side
impedes the player as a wall does: its speed across becomes 0 and
it moves one pixel away, unless it is already moving away. Super
Mario Bros.' PlatformSideCollisions calls ImpedePlayerMove. Default
off: a touch doesn't move the player.

stand.description:
A falling player lands on the entity's hitbox top instead of
stomping it, and rides it while it moves: `enemy.stood_on` fires on
landing. The touch below the top is still `otherwise`.

stomp_depth.description:
A falling player whose bottom row is within this many rows of the
top of this entity's hitbox stomps it: `enemy.stomped` fires and the
entity is removed, unless `keep_on_stomp`. Without it the entity
can't be stomped.

touch_edges.description:
Since 0.4.14: the touch's test takes each hitbox one pixel wider and
taller, so two that only meet at their edges touch. Super Mario
Bros.' SprObjectCollisionCore compares a box's left and right as
offsets from BoundBoxCtrlData, each a pixel in the box, and counts
equal as a touch. Default off: hitboxes touch when they share a pixel.

Cost.description:
Feature `cost.frame`: a frame's CPU cycles in the original, `base`
plus each term whose tests hold, times the bodies of its `per` kind
that pass its `per_tests` when it has one. The simulation sums it at the end of each
frame, before the `hook_last` hooks, adds what the hooks added
(`ExtCx::add_cycles`), and a hook reads the sum
(`ExtCx::frame_cycles`): Donkey Kong's idle loop steps its random
register in the cycles the frame's work leaves.

terms.description: The terms, each a routine's part or a branch of one.

CostTerm.description: One term of a [`Cost`]: `cycles` on a frame every test holds.

per.description:
An entity kind: the term counts once for each active body of it
that passes `per_tests`.

per_tests.description: Tests on each body of `per`: its `ext` words (`word`).

routine.description:
The routine or branch it stands for, by the code's address, and
why: informative.

CostTest.description: A test of a [`CostTerm`]: one thing it reads, in a range.

at.description:
With `counter`: read as the frame started (`start`, the default) or
as it ends (`end`), for a routine that runs before or after the
frame's other work changes it.

at_least.description: The value is at least this.

held.description: An input action held this frame (1) or not (0).

held_before.description: An input action held the frame before (1) or not (0).

pad.description:
Feature `cost.frame_pad`: an input action's bits on controller 1 as
pressed this frame (1) or not (0), before `keep_direction`, a turn's
controller or a hook's held actions: the pad a controller routine
reads, which runs on every frame of an attract demo too.

state.description:
A game machine's state (`machine:state`) as the frame started: 1 in
it, 0 not.

Counter.description:
A number the game keeps: score, coins, lives, time. It starts at
`start` when the game does, and a level's `counters` set it when the
level starts; restarting a level leaves it alone otherwise.

high_of.description:
Feature `counter.high_of`: the counter keeps the highest value the
named counter has had, raised as that one changes, as a top score
does (Donkey Kong's $21-$23, which $D03E raises from the score after
every award).

max.description:
It never goes above this: a change past it stops at it, or with
`wrap`, goes on from `min` (or 0) and fires `<counter>.wrapped`.

min.description: It never goes below this. Reaching it fires `<counter>.reached_min`.

restarts_clock.description:
Feature `counter.restarts_clock`: a level start that sets the counter (the level's
`counters`) also starts its `every` clocks over, as Super Mario
Bros.' InitializeArea clears GameTimerCtrlTimer with the other frame
timers when an area starts.

runs_when_frozen.description:
Its `every` changes go on counting while the world is frozen
(Super Mario Bros.' color rotation, which runs while Mario dies).
Since core 0.4.8.

shift.description:
Since core 0.4.20: the counter is a shift register: it steps every frame the `counters`
system runs (Super Mario Bros.' PseudoRandomBitReg, which the NMI
rotates every frame).

CounterShift.description:
A linear feedback shift register in a counter's low `bits` bits: each
step moves them one bit down, and the top bit becomes the exclusive-or of
the old bits at `taps`.

CounterTest.description: A test on one of the model's counters. Presentation only.

at_least.description: The counter is at least this.

DecelBand.description: A walking rate from a speed up (since 0.4.2).

Defeat.description:
What a defeat leaves (0.4.12): a body of another entity at the same
place, which keeps the defeated one's numbered slot until it leaves.

rise.description: Pixels it moves up at once.

speed.description: The whole part of its speed up and down; the fraction is kept.

DespawnAt.description: What despawning by the view measures (core 0.4.10).

oneOf.description: The far edge behind the view, the near edge ahead of it.
The entity's position, in whole pixels, both ways.
The standard NES controller.

An arcade cabinet's controls for one player: the coin slot, the
one-player start button, a joystick and one button. The runtime
protocol's bits are coin, start1, right, left, down, up and
button1 from bit 0 (gp-arcade's order, MAME's oracle log's).

Draw.description:
How a level is drawn ahead of the view (Super Mario Bros.' area
parser): when it starts, every column left of `ahead` pixels past the
view's far edge; then, each time the view's near edge passes a whole
`step` (counted from the level's left edge), the next `step` pixels of
columns, one column every `every` frames from that frame. Since core
0.4.10.

ahead.description: Pixels drawn past the view's far edge when the level starts.

every.description: Frames from one column of a set to the next.

pause.description:
Frames after a set starts on which no entity appears by the view
but `drawn` ones (Super Mario Bros.' enemy loop leaves while
AreaParserTaskNum is 7).

step.description: Pixels of columns in a set: a whole number of tiles.

oneOf.description: The cell a head hit took on the event's frame.
The event's entity's position.

EffectOrder.description:
Feature `present.effect_order`: an effect takes the table's sprites
from `at + step * k`, k being the place of the counter its phase took
among the phase's `until_counters` (the points sprite a game with two
gave it), else 0.

at.description: The first hardware sprite's number in the table (0 to 63).

step.description: Hardware sprites each of its places takes (default 4).

EffectPhase.description: One phase of an effect: its pictures, how it moves and when it ends.

cells.description: Each tile's flips, palette and place, as a sprite's `cells`.

every.description: Frames each picture shows for. Default 1.

frames.description:
The pictures, each a list of tile numbers row by row, shown in turn
by the game's frames.

motion.description:
How it moves up and down. The first phase's speed is the start's;
a later phase with a motion starts at its own speed.

palette.description: A sprite palette of the level's palettes, as a sprite's.

rise_every.description: Rises a pixel on each frame whose count is a multiple of this.

until_counter.description:
Ends on the frame after one on which this counter is 0 or less, as
a game that hides a sprite by a timer it reads before the frame's
timers step (feature `present.effects.until_counter`).

until_counters.description:
As `until_counter`, with the one of these counters that is highest
as the phase starts: the timer the event's picture took, for a game
that shows it in whichever of several slots is free (feature
`present.effects.until_counters`). Donkey Kong's points sprites:
`points_timer` and `points_timer_2` ($41, $42; $CFC6 takes the
first free).

until_gone.description:
Ends on the frame the event's entity is gone, and the next phase
starts on that frame (feature `present.effects.until_gone`).

until_speed.description: Ends on the frame its speed's whole part reaches this.

while_frozen.description:
Goes on while a state freezes the world, as a game object the
freeze doesn't stop; its pictures and rise count the world's
frames.

with_camera.description: Moves across as the camera does, so it keeps its place on screen.

EffectPresent.description:
A short-lived picture an event starts (the feature `present.effects`): its phases in
turn, then gone. Presentation only.

offset.description:
The picture's top left in pixels from the cell's top left or the
entity's position.

Entity.description: Core entity fields. Other keys are components of the genre extensions the model declares, each checked against its extension's schema.

bounce.description: Since 0.4.10: bouncing off the ground at a point, and leaving.

despawn_ahead.description:
Its own `despawn_ahead`, in place of the level's: Super Mario Bros.'
cannon bill flies off to the right and goes past the same line
(OffscreenBoundsCheck), where a level's would also take what a start
or a layout leaves out there.

despawn_behind.description:
Its own `despawn_behind`, in place of the level's: Super Mario
Bros.' piranha plants and hammer brothers go sooner than the rest
(OffscreenBoundsCheck). Since core 0.4.10.

despawn_behind_wrap.description:
`[from, behind]`: while the view's left edge is `from` or more into
its 256-pixel page, `behind` stands in for `despawn_behind`. Super
Mario Bros.' OffscreenBoundsCheck adds 57 to the edge's low byte and
the carry out of that takes a whole page off the limit.

ext.description:
A hand-written behavior behind the `ext` boundary, by name, for what
the components can't say. It runs in the system of the entity's
role: `platformer.player` for the player, `platformer.enemies` for
the rest.

ext_params.description:
The numbers the `ext` hook reads, by name: speeds, timers, offsets.
Each is a fact with evidence, like any other, and a state's `set`
can change them. Only an entity with `ext` has them.

ext_rows.description:
Feature `entity.ext_rows`: more tables the `ext` hook reads, by
name, each a `rows` asset slot whose rows' numbers, in order, are
one table, for a hook that reads by address a span the model lifts
as rows. Only an entity with `ext` has them.

ext_tables.description:
The tables the `ext` hook reads, by name: each a column of one of
the model's `table` asset slots, as `<slot>.<column>`, so indexed
data the hook needs is lifted from the original like any asset.
Only an entity with `ext` has them.

extra_slots.description:
More of a level's `spawn_slots` it takes besides its own, numbered
slots included: Super Mario Bros.' long firebar, for which
DuplicateEnemyObj takes the next free enemy slot.

hitbox.description:
The box that touches other entities and tiles, from the entity's
position (its top left corner).

hook_first.description:
Feature `entity.hook_first`: its `ext` hook runs at the start of the
`platformer.player` system, before the player moves, rather than in
`platformer.enemies` after it: a game routine that sets what the
player's routine reads. Donkey Kong's attract demo ($EBDA) puts the
script's direction in $56 just before Mario's routine reads it.

hook_frame_start.description:
Feature `entity.hook_frame_start`: its `ext` hook's `frame_start`
runs at the start of every frame, before the first system, frozen
or not, as a game's NMI runs its sound driver before anything else.
Donkey Kong's sound driver steps there.

hook_last.description:
Feature `entity.hook_last`: its `ext` hook runs once at the end of
every frame, after every system, frozen, stopped or a level start
alike, and not in `platformer.enemies`: a game's idle loop, which
runs after the frame's work whatever it was. Donkey Kong's ($C7E1)
steps its random register once a pass while it waits for the NMI.

hook_through_stops.description:
Feature `entity.hook_through_stops`: its `ext` hook still runs on a
frame a state's `stops` lists the system it runs in (not under a
`freeze`). Donkey Kong's oil drum keeps the game's frame timers,
which count on through a death while the fires stand still.

invincible.description: Since 0.4.10, a player's: invincible while a counter holds.

launcher.description:
Since 0.4.28: it fires another entity on its own timer and a shift
counter's bits.

locks.description:
A player's actions that do nothing while a counter holds (feature
`power.locks`): Donkey Kong's hammer, held while its timer runs,
takes away jumping and climbing.

machine.description:
The entity's own state machine (small and big, walking and in its
shell). Each instance runs its own copy. A state's `set` changes
the entity's fields while in it.

no_slot.description:
Takes none of a level's `spawn_slots`: Super Mario Bros.' hammers
and a firebar's fireballs, which the game keeps outside its enemy
slots. Since core 0.4.10.

role.description: What the entity is for (docs/model.md lists the roles).

stream.description: A level marker that sends entities in from past the view's edge.

tile_collision.description: Stops against solid tiles and stands on them.

tile_hitbox.description: The box that touches tiles, when it isn't `hitbox`.

touch_points.description:
A player's points, in pixels from its position, that a
`contact.near` tests. Super Mario Bros.' FirebarCollision tests
y+24 for small Mario and y, y+12 and y+24 for big Mario, 4 pixels in
from his left. Default none: no `contact.near` touches this player.

EntryRef.description:
One entry of an asset that holds a list per entry, such as one area's
objects.

entry.description: The entry's `name` in the asset map.

refs.description: What supports it: files with line numbers, baselines, recordings.

Exit.description: A way from one level to another.

enter.description:
Where the player comes out in `to`, its top left corner. Without it,
the player's spawn there.

keep.description:
The player's coordinate on this axis keeps its place in the view
across the exit (its position less the view's corner), as a room
change that scrolls does; `enter` gives the other one.

scroll.description:
The exit takes this many frames, as a room change that scrolls the
view does: the world is frozen and the player held until they're
over.

start.description:
Taking it starts `to` as a level, as `next-level` does (its counter
values, `level.started`, and `restart-level` starts it again),
rather than entering it as a room of the level being played. A
pipe intro's pipe and a warp zone's pipes are.

take.description:
What takes it. Without it the exit is only in the progression
graph and nothing in the game takes it.

Fall.description:
Falling for an entity that doesn't jump: `gravity` is added to its
vertical speed every frame, up to `max_fall`.

feet.description:
Since 0.4.19: the columns where the ground is looked for, in pixels
from the entity's x, as `jump.feet`. Without them it is every column
of the tile hitbox. Super Mario Bros.' ChkUnderEnemy tests one point,
x + 8, so a goomba drops off a ledge once its middle is past the
edge.

max_fall_from_half.description:
Since 0.4.3: the fall limit acts from one half past it, as
`jump.max_fall_from_half`.

move_first.description:
The position moves by the old vertical speed before gravity is
added, as Super Mario Bros. does, rather than after.

stands_still.description:
Since 0.4.19: a body on the ground takes no gravity. It only looks
for the ground, and falls from the frame after it has gone. Placed
in a numbered slot it takes the slot's height fraction (since
0.4.21), and on the ground no speed from the slot. Super Mario
Bros.' enemy in state 0 skips MoveD_EnemyVertically, ChkForRedKoopa's
change to state 1 moves it from the next frame, nothing clears
Enemy_YMF_Dummy, and SetBBox runs on into InitVStf.

Fixed.description: A fixed-point number with 16 fraction bits: an integer, or an exact decimal string such as "0.25". Floats are refused.

Fly.description:
Moving sideways at a steady speed, through tiles: a bullet or a
swimming fish. Since 0.4.10 it may have `fall` too, for a projectile
thrown in an arc.

heading.description: Which way it goes; default toward the player when it spawns.

keep_speed.description:
Since 0.4.10: it keeps the speed across it has (one a start carries
from the original, or `shoot.vx`), and takes `speed` the way it
faces only while that is 0. Super Mario Bros.' fireball moves by
whatever Fireball_X_Speed holds.

speed.description: Pixels per frame, without its sign.

under.description:
Since 0.4.13: a player whose top edge is at or below this y passes
under the goal and doesn't reach it.

x.description: The player's left edge reaching this x.

Ground.description:
Feature `level.ground`: each row of `runs` is a run of boxes, its first
five bytes x, y, shape, the step across from one box to the next (a
signed byte) and the count; each box is `rise` pixels above the last,
and x and y wrap as bytes. The shape divided by `shape_step` is a row
of `shapes`, whose four bytes are the box's left, top, right and bottom
from its place, edges included. A body on the ground keeps its height
while its feet, the columns `feet` from its x on the row under its tile
hitbox, meet a box; once they meet none it moves to the nearest row a
pixel or two up or down whose box they meet. Donkey Kong's walk tests
Mario's feet box ($C186: his sprite +8 to +10, +17 down) against the
girder pieces of his row ($D91A, the runs at $C08C, each piece a pixel
higher) after each move across and steps a pixel when it finds none
($D8EB).

bodies.description:
Feature `level.ground_bodies`: entities whose box is ground too, so
the ground can move. A ground test meets the level's boxes first,
then these bodies' boxes in the bodies' order. A body whose test
meets one of these rides it: it moves by the same step whenever
that body moves, and it stays standing without a test until it
moves across or leaves the ground. The ride ends at the next test
that meets no box at all (the walk's after a move across, each
frame of a jump after its takeoff, a ledge fall's); a test that
meets one of the level's boxes leaves it as it was. Donkey Kong's
75m: when the stage's boxes hold nothing ($D316), $D326 tests the
six elevator platforms against Mario's feet box and sets $DA by the
column it meets, or clears it when it meets none; $E834 then moves
Mario's sprite with the column on each of its steps while $DA holds.

boxes.description:
Feature `level.ground_boxes`: each row of `runs` is one box, its
first three bytes x, y and shape, with no step across or count.
Donkey Kong's ground on every stage but 25m ($D2E2 reads the
stage's rows through the pointer at $C46B and tests Mario's feet box
against each, $D8AD; 75m's at $C20C).

land.description:
Feature `level.ground_land`: a jump falling (its vertical speed 0
or more) lands on the first box its feet meet on a row from this
many pixels above the row under its tile hitbox down to that row,
wherever it was the frame before, and the tiles don't land it. A
ledge fall (`jump.ledge_fall`) lands the same way, where it is.
Donkey Kong's jump tests Mario's feet box, +10 to +12 down from his
height, against the girder pieces in their list's order ($D5CC,
$D2CB, $D91A) and puts him on the first it meets ($D5D3); his fall
off a girder's end tests the same box and dies where it meets one
($D6BC).

land_rising.description:
Feature `level.ground_land_rising`: with `land`, a jump lands on a
box its feet meet on any frame after its takeoff, rising too. Donkey
Kong's jump runs its ground test ($D5CC) on every frame but the
takeoff's ($D5BB) whichever way the arc goes, so a jump whose feet
rise into a box's top lands there.

GroundBody.description:
Feature `level.ground_bodies`: an entity kind whose bodies are ground,
and its box: left, top, right and bottom from the body's place, edges
included. Donkey Kong's elevator platform is the box at $C2C8: its
sprite's x to x + 18 on the row under its y ($D326 with $2A).

GroundOnEnter.description: What entering a state does to an entity's standing (core 0.4.13).

Guard.description: A comparison of a counter with a number.

Halfway.description:
A level's checkpoint (feature `level.halfway`): when `restart-level` starts the
level again while the first camera's x is at least `from`, that camera
starts at `from` and the player at `at`, and the entities come as the
view reaches them from there. Super Mario Bros.' PlayerLoseLife sets
HalfwayPage from HalfwayPageNybbles when ScreenLeft_PageLoc has reached
the level's page, and InitializeArea starts the area at that page.

Head.description:
A head point (since 0.4.5). After the vertical move, while the entity
rises (its vertical speed below 0), its y is at least `above` and at
least `row_from` pixels into its tile row, the cell `point` is in
decides: a cell that stops movement sets the vertical speed's whole
part to its hit's `speed`, fires its `event` for the entity and turns
into `becomes`. The entity isn't moved. The tile hitbox still stops
the entity from the sides and lands it, but no longer stops a rise.

above.description: No head test while the entity's y is less than this.

busy_while.description:
Feature `head.busy_while`: while this holds, every cell that stops movement is
hit as a `solid` one: no event, no change to the cell. Super Mario
Bros.' PlayerBGCollision reads BlockBounceTimer, which a block hit
sets to 16 frames, and takes no block hit while it runs (NYSpd).

hits.description:
What a hit does by the cell's kind, first match. A cell that stops
movement and isn't listed sets the speed's whole part to 0.

keep_fraction.description:
A hit sets the speed's whole part and keeps its fraction, rather
than setting the whole speed.

point.description: The point, x and y from the entity's position, in whole pixels.

row_from.description:
A head test only when the entity's y, in the tile row it's in, is
at least this many pixels down (y mod the tile size).

HeadAbove.description:
What a head hit does to the cell above the one hit (feature `head.above`): when
that cell is `tile`, it becomes `becomes` and `event` fires for the
entity. Super Mario Bros.' BumpBlock and BrickShatter call
CheckTopOfBlock, which takes a coin sitting on the block that was hit.

HeadHit.description: What a head hit on one kind of cell does.

above.description: Feature `head.above`: what the hit does to the cell above.

event.description:
An event fired for the entity: the core's, an extension's or the
model's own.

hold.description:
Since 0.4.6: frames after the hit's frame that the cell stays
solid, as a plain `solid` cell, before it becomes `becomes` (or the
kind it was, without one), as in a game that keeps a bumped block's
cell solid while the block bounces. A body that hits it meanwhile
gets the `solid` hit. It is world state, counted down on frames
that aren't frozen.

speed.description: The vertical speed's whole part after the hit (positive: down).

tile.description:
A kind that stops movement: `solid`, `coin_block`, `item_block` or
`brick`.

events.description:
Events of the model's own, which `ext` hooks fire and transitions
and counter changes name, such as `ladder.grabbed`. One fired with
an entity concerns only that instance's machine; one fired without
concerns every instance.

extensions.description: The genre extensions the model uses, with their versions.

features.description:
The optional features the model uses, by name, such as
`launcher` or `contact.touch_edges` ([`crate::features`]). A reader
refuses a model listing one it doesn't know. Without the list the
features are derived from the fields the model sets; with it, each
one used must be listed.

frame_rate.description:
Frames per second as presented: "60", or a ratio such as
"39375000/655171" (the NTSC NES). The simulation counts frames and
never reads it.

name.description: A short name: letters, digits and `_`.

profile.description:
The profile the model was built in (core 0.4.5), such as "normal":
set only by applying one from the template's `profiles.toml`
([`crate::profile`]), never in a `model.toml`. Absent, the model is
its base profile, "retro". Runtimes put it in the state hash.

schema.description: The core schema version the model is written for, such as "0.4.1".

source.description:
The source ID the model was made from, as in sources/*.toml or an
asset map, when there is one.

start_level.description: The level the game starts in. Needed when there's more than one.

systems.description:
The order the systems run in each frame: every system of the core
and of each declared extension, once each ([`CORE_SYSTEMS`]).

oneOf.description: Toward the player when it spawns.

counter.description: The player's: the counter that holds its hit points.

damage_from.description:
Damage taken from each hitting entity, by entity name, instead of
its `hits.damage`.

defeat.description:
Since 0.4.12: what a defeat by a hit or a touch leaves in its place,
instead of nothing.

invulnerable.description: Frames after a hurt in which no hurt counts.

points.description: Any other entity's: its hit points when it appears.

shield.description:
Hits do nothing (the hitter still goes, unless `hits.keep`): a
shield, usually set by a state.

Hidden.description:
Bodies not drawn while one of the rule states holds and every counter
test does (feature `present.hidden`). Presentation only.

hud.description:
The HUD not drawn either: its layer, its fields and its sprites,
as Donkey Kong's 100m ending blanks the status rows ($C6E4, entry
$0A of $C03C). With no `kinds`, only the HUD.

kinds.description:
The entity types hidden, whichever layer they are drawn in. None
given: the console's sprite layer, every body but those drawn as
name-table tiles and the HUD's sprites, as `present.sprites_off`,
unless `hud` is given.

when.description: The model's counters in ranges, each of which must hold too.

Hits.description:
Hitting other entities: a projectile, or a thrown enemy. Touching an
entity with `health` whose role is in `roles` takes `damage` from it
(or its `damage_from` for this entity) and fires `enemy.hit` for it;
one out of hit points fires `enemy.defeated` and leaves the level. The
hitter leaves too, unless `keep`.

every.description:
Since 0.4.10: hits are tested only on frames whose number less
`phase` is a multiple of this, as `contact.every` (Super Mario
Bros.' FireballEnemyCollision runs on even frames).

move_first.description:
Since 0.4.10: the hitter moves (its components, as the enemies
system moves it) in the contact system, just before its hits are
tested, and not in the enemies system, so it hits the others where
they were before they move. Super Mario Bros. runs FireballObjCore,
which moves a fireball and tests it against the enemies, ahead of
its enemy loop.

roles.description: The roles it hits. Default `enemy` and `boss`.

Hop.description:
Jumping again on landing: the vertical speed becomes `speed` (negative,
up) whenever the entity lands. Needs `fall`.

every.description:
Since 0.4.1: it hops only on frames whose number, plus `phase` times
the body's index, is a multiple of `every`: a hop on a beat.
Standing on other frames, it waits.

land_first.description:
Since 0.4.8: the landing comes before the move, as Super Mario
Bros.' EnemyJump runs in EnemyToBGCollisionDet before
MoveJumpingEnemy. At the start of its turn, standing on ground
(its bottom row in a tile that stops it) with its speed's whole
part anything but -2, -1 or 0 (the game adds 2 to Enemy_Y_Speed and
compares it with 3 unsigned), it is placed on that tile's top, its
height's fraction kept, and takes the hop's speed; then it moves by
its `fall`, and a move into the ground doesn't stop it.

land_while_stopped.description:
Since 0.4.26: with `land_first`, the landing still happens on a frame a freeze or
a state's `stops` or `stops_at_once` keeps the enemies from moving,
as Super Mario Bros.' RunNormalEnemies runs EnemyToBGCollisionDet
before its TimerControl check, which skips only EnemyMovementSubs.

pattern.description:
Since 0.4.1: the speeds of its hops in turn, from the first, then
again from the start (three small hops and a big one), instead of
`speed`. The count of hops is kept in the body's mechanic words, so
an entity with a pattern has no `ext` hook.

Hud.description:
A heads-up display: fixed tiles and fields bound to counters and the
level, drawn in screen positions over the view. Its role is `hud`, for
themes.

field.description: Text drawn from the game's state.

font.description: A slot of kind `font`: the tile for each character the fields show.

layer.description:
An entry of a `screen-text` slot: the HUD's fixed tiles and their
palettes, such as the status bar's names.

size.description:
Width and height in tiles of the part of the screen the HUD covers,
from the top left. Default the whole screen.

sprite.description:
Pictures the game draws as sprites over its status bar, such as the
one it uses to split the screen. Since core 0.4.7.

tiles.description: A slot of kind `tiles`: the tiles the HUD is drawn with.

HudField.description: One piece of HUD text: a counter, the level's label or fixed text.

at.description:
Column and row of its first character, in tiles from the screen's
top left.

counter.description: A counter, by name, shown as a number.

digits.description:
For a counter: how many digits, padded on the left with `pad`. A
number too long for them shows its last digits.

divide.description:
For a counter: shown divided by this, rounding down, for a game
that keeps a number's last digit fixed in the HUD's layer (a score
whose ones are always 0). Default 1.

pad.description: The character a counter is padded with. Default "0".

palette.description:
The background palette its tiles use, or with `sprite` the sprite
palette. Default 0.

sprite.description:
Drawn as sprites, one 8x8 sprite a character, as a game that puts
its counters in the sprite table does (Moss Hop): the screen
measure counts its pixels as the sprite layer's, like a HUD sprite.

when.description:
Feature `present.hud.field_when`: drawn only while every one of
these counter tests holds. Donkey Kong draws player 2's label and
score only in a two-player game, and each player's score in its own
place whoever's turn it is.

HudSprite.description:
One sprite tile fixed on the screen, drawn over the HUD. The screen
measure counts its pixels as the sprite layer's.

at.description: The tile's top left corner, in screen pixels.

behind.description:
Behind the background, as the NES's priority bit puts a sprite: its
pixels show only where the HUD's fixed layer draws nothing.

tile.description: The tile's number in that slot.

tiles.description: A slot of kind `tiles`: the sprite tiles.

actions.description: Action names to buttons. Extensions read actions by name.

keep_direction.description:
Feature `input.keep_direction`: the pad's directions are latched as
a game filters them. A direction that acted on the frame before and
is still held stays the only one, and newly held ones wait until it
is let go; with none of them held, every direction held acts.
Donkey Kong's pad routine ($F549) keeps the old directions that are
still held, so Up added while walking left doesn't climb until Left
is let go.

turn.description:
Feature `input.turn`: in a game whose players take turns, the
player whose turn it is plays from their own controller. While the
counter is k, these actions read controller k + 1; every other
action reads controller 1. Donkey Kong's player routine reads the
pad at $15 + 2 times the player in $52 ($D175), so player 2 plays
from controller 2, while Start and Select are read from controller
1 only ($CF42, $CE8B).

Invincible.description:
Since 0.4.10: a player that is invincible while `while` holds (a
counter compared with a number, as a transition's `if` is). While it
does, a touch does the toucher's `contact.invincible` instead of a
stomp or its `otherwise`: by default an entity whose touch would hurt
or kill the player, or kick it, is defeated (Super Mario Bros.'
StarInvincibleTimer: CheckForPUpCollision jumps to ShellOrBlockDefeat
before HandlePECollisions looks at a stomp).

Jump.description: Jumping and falling. Vertical speed is positive downward.

action.description: The input action that jumps, newly pressed while standing.

bands.description:
Jumps that depend on the horizontal speed at takeoff: the first band
whose `below` is above the speed gives `speed`, `gravity` and
`gravity_held` for the whole jump, and a speed at or above every
band's uses the values above. In order of `below`.

buffer_frames.description: Frames a jump pressed in the air is remembered until landing.

collide_y.description:
Since 0.4.8: the entity meets tiles (landing, the head, the feet's
depth and the wall points) only while its y, in whole pixels, is at
least the first and below the second; elsewhere it goes through
them. Super Mario Bros.' PlayerBGCollision does nothing while
Mario's high byte is off the screen or his y is $cf or more, so he
falls into a pit past the ground's side.

coyote_frames.description: Frames after walking off a ledge in which a jump still works.

fatal_drop.description:
Feature `jump.fatal_drop`: a jump that lands this many pixels or
more below its takeoff kills the player, when its `land_hold` ends
(on landing without one). Mechanic word 3 keeps the takeoff height.
Donkey Kong sets $95 to $FF 16 px below the takeoff and kills after
the 4-frame hold.

fatal_drop_in_air.description:
Feature `jump.fatal_drop_in_air`: with `fatal_drop`, mechanic word
3 keeps the height after the takeoff frame's move, and the drop is
tested on every later frame in the air, on the height the frame's
move reaches before a landing puts the body on the ground. Once it
holds, the word is -1000 and the landing kills. Donkey Kong's jump
routine keeps $95 from $01 after the arc's first step ($D570-$D57C,
$D5EA), sets it to $FF once the step's height less 16 is at or past
it ($D5BF-$D5CA), before the landing test ($D5CC), and kills on $FF
as the hold ends ($D615).

feet.description:
Since 0.4.5: ground points, the columns (x from the entity's
position, whole pixels) where the tile hitbox's bottom row looks
for ground, instead of across the hitbox's width. A machine state's
`set` can change them.

gravity.description:
Added to the vertical speed every frame, on the ground and off it
(off it only, with `no_gravity_on_ground`).

gravity_held.description:
Gravity instead while the action is held and the entity is rising,
for jumps whose height depends on how long the button is held.
Without it, holding longer changes nothing.

head.description:
Since 0.4.5: one point over the head decides what a rise into a
tile does, instead of the tile hitbox's top edge. A machine state's
`set` can change it (a bigger player's head is higher).

keep_fall_gravity.description:
Since 0.4.6: the entity's fall gravity is kept from its last jump
(its band's `gravity`, or `gravity` above), after it lands too, and
a fall that isn't a jump (off a ledge, or from ground that left)
uses it, as in a game that keeps one falling force for the player
and sets it only when a jump starts. The held phase still uses
`gravity_held`. It is world state (`fall_gravity`), which a state
mapping can read from the original.

land_depth.description:
Since 0.4.5: a landing on a tile only while the tile hitbox's
bottom row is less than this many pixels into the tile. Deeper, the
entity doesn't land: it is pushed one pixel back the way it last
moved, as against a wall, its speed across becomes 0, and its wall
points aren't tested that frame.

land_hold.description:
Feature `jump.land_hold`: for this many frames after the frame a
jump lands, the entity neither walks, jumps nor takes a ladder; it
stands. Mechanic word 2 counts the frames left. Donkey Kong keeps
Mario in his jump state for 4 frames after landing ($94 from $F0 to
$F4), and the jump routine runs no ladder test (clear-25m clip 1,
frames 3086-3089).

land_keeps_fraction.description:
Since 0.4.5: landing on a tile sets the whole part of the height
to the tile's top and keeps its fraction, and a jump's takeoff
clears the fraction, as in a game that masks the height's whole
byte on landing and keeps its fraction byte apart.

ledge_fall.description:
Feature `jump.ledge_fall`: a fall that isn't a jump (walking off a
ledge) drops straight down at a fixed speed, and may kill on landing.

max_fall_from_half.description:
Since 0.4.3: the fall limit acts only once the speed's whole part
is at least `max_fall` and its fraction at least one half, and then
sets the speed to `max_fall`, so a fall goes a little past the limit
on some frames. `max_fall` must be whole.

move_first.description:
The position moves by the old vertical speed before gravity is
added, as Super Mario Bros. does, rather than after.

no_gravity_on_ground.description:
Since 0.4.5: a frame that starts on the ground and doesn't start a
jump adds no gravity and doesn't move the entity up or down, as in a
game that moves a standing player only across. If the ground under
it has gone by the end of the frame it is in the air, and gravity
starts on the next frame.

pickup.description:
Since 0.4.18: points that take a tile by touching it, as a coin. A
machine state's `set` can change them.

release_cap.description:
Once the action isn't held, a rise faster than this (negative: up)
is cut to it, every frame: a jump cut short by letting go.

speed.description: The vertical speed a jump sets (negative: up).

start_fall_gravity.description:
Since 0.4.6, with `keep_fall_gravity`: the fall gravity before the
entity's first jump, from when it is placed at a level start or
through an exit. Without it, `gravity`.

takeoff_fraction.description:
Feature `jump.takeoff_fraction`: a takeoff sets the height's
fraction to this (from 0, below 1), as a game that keeps a jump's
height in a fraction byte of its own and starts it at a set value.
Donkey Kong's jump routine starts its fraction at $F0.

JumpBand.description:
A jump band: the values a jump uses when the horizontal speed at
takeoff is below `below`.

below.description:
The horizontal speed (without its sign) the band reaches up to, not
included.

KeepRow.description:
A row of a camera's `keep_in_view_rows`: from `rows[0]` to `rows[1]`
(whole pixels down, both in), the bounds are `bounds`.

Knockback.description:
Being knocked back by a hurt that counts: for `frames` frames the entity
moves `speed` a frame against the way it faces, its run input ignored,
and on the first its vertical speed becomes `rise`.

Ladders.description:
Feature `level.ladders`: each row of `places` is a ladder, its first
three bytes its x, its y and its shape; the shape divided by
`shape_step` is a row of `shapes`, whose four bytes are the box's left,
top, right and bottom from the ladder's x and y, edges included.
Donkey Kong keeps each stage's ladders this way ($C0E3 and $C10B for
25m).

end.description:
Feature `level.ladder_lists`: the byte that ends a list read by
`places_at`. Default 254 ($FE, Donkey Kong's).

places_at.description:
Feature `level.ladder_lists`: `places` names a byte table's column
(`slot.column`) that holds the game's own list, rows of three bytes
from this index up to a row that starts with `end`.

shapes_at.description:
Feature `level.ladder_lists`: `shapes` names a byte table's column
whose rows of four bytes start at this index.

Launcher.description:
Since 0.4.28: a launcher, an object that fires the entity `fires` on its
own timer and a shift counter's bits, aimed at the player's side (Super
Mario Bros.' bullet bill cannons: SetupCannon, ProcessCannons and
BulletBillHandler).

The level's launchers keep `table` entries. One that appears (a `drawn`
spawn, as its column is drawn) takes the entry the counter `next` names,
ending the launcher that had it and keeping that one's timer, and moves
`next` on, back to 0 after the last. One placed left of `from_x` takes its
entry and fires nothing, so it has no body. A launcher that appears is
picked from the next frame on (the area parser runs after the enemies).

Each frame after the other enemies, the level's first `slots` numbered
slots (`slot_rest`) take a turn each, the last first. A slot that holds a
shot gives the shot its turn: shots move there, not with the other
enemies. A free slot reads a byte of `counter` from bit `at`, `slot_step`
bits lower for each slot after the first, and'ed with `mask` (`hard_mask`
in a level with `hard_spawns`). A value below `table` picks that entry's
launcher: a timer above 0 counts down by 1, and at 0 it fires, unless the
enemies are frozen. The shot appears at the launcher moved by `offset`,
in that slot with the slot's rest fraction across, and doesn't move that
frame; the timer is set to `rearm`. A freeze counts timers down too.

On its first turn a shot goes if it is past the view's right edge,
`behind` pixels or more left of its left edge, or within `near` pixels of
the player. The test is on the whole-pixel difference modulo `near_wrap`
(none when 0), with 1 added when the shot is at or right of the player:
`(d + near + carry) mod wrap < 2 near`. Otherwise it faces the player's
side and flies. The launcher keeps its timer and entry in mechanic words 0
and 1, and a shot keeps "aimed" in its word 0, so neither has an `ext`
hook.

Leap.description:
Leaping again and again from a start point (since 0.4.1): placed at
`from` (a y, or where it's placed without one), it leaps at `speed`
(negative is up; a drop starts down) and is pulled by `gravity`, on frames whose number
is a multiple of `every`, falling at most `max_fall`, through tiles.
With `rise`, it first rises at `rise.speed` until `rise.height` above
the start, then leaps. It starts again from the start when its wait is
over (`interval` frames times one of `waits`, drawn at random as the
leap starts) or once it is `below` pixels under the start. A lava
bubble, or a log that drops in a waterfall. The wait and the phase are
kept in the body's mechanic words 0 and 1, so it has no `ext` hook.

beat.description:
Since 0.4.17: a counter with an `every`. The wait counts that
shared beat's ticks instead of `interval` frames, and a new body
waits one tick before its first leap.

draw.description:
Since 0.4.26: a byte of a shift counter picks the wait and the speed's fraction,
instead of the generator. Needs `beat`.

keep_fraction.description: Since 0.4.17: a new leap keeps the fraction of the height.

move_first.description: Since 0.4.17: the old speed moves it and gravity comes after.

place_on_appear.description:
Since 0.4.26: a body is at its start point on the frame it appears,
as InitPodoboo places it while the area parser fills the slot.

LeapDraw.description:
Where a leap reads its random byte: `counter`, a counter with a `shift`,
from bit `at`, `slot_step` bits lower for each numbered slot after the
first. The byte modulo the length of `waits` picks the wait, and the byte
or'd with `fraction` is the launch speed's fraction, in 256ths, added to
`speed`.

LeapRise.description: A slow rise before a leap.

LeaveView.description:
Leaving the level once it is off the view (since 0.4.1): removed on the
first frame its position along `axis` (whole pixels from the view's
near edge) is under `margin`, or at or past the view's size less
`margin`. A projectile that is gone once it leaves the screen.

bottom_margin.description:
Since 0.4.24: it also leaves at or past the view's height less this
margin, whatever the `axis`. Super Mario Bros.' fireball goes at
height 240 (0 here), where FBall_OffscreenBits' vertical half sets
a bit FireballObjCore tests, as well as past the sides.

far_margin.description:
Since 0.4.10: the margin at the view's far edge (right or bottom),
when it isn't `margin`. Super Mario Bros.' fireball goes once any
of it is off the screen: its left edge past the left, or its right
edge, 8 pixels on, past the right.

LedgeFall.description:
A fall off a ledge at a fixed speed (feature `jump.ledge_fall`). The
frame the body walks off it moves `first` pixels down (or `speed`), and
`speed` on each frame after, with no gravity and no move across; the
run gets no input, and a step counter (`run.step_cycle`) steps on each
frame of the fall. With `kills` the landing kills the player. Donkey
Kong's state 8 ($D697): 2 a frame, 3 on the first, and death on landing.

Level.description: Core level fields. Other keys are components of the genre extensions the model declares, each checked against its extension's schema.

appear_still.description:
An entity that appears by the view first moves on the frame after,
as a game that fills an enemy slot instead of running it does.
Since core 0.4.10.

camera.description:
How the cameras move in this level, where it differs from each
camera's own settings.

counters.description:
Values counters take when the level starts, by counter name, such as
the time limit.

despawn_after_move.description:
`despawn_behind` and `despawn_ahead` are tested after the enemies
system has moved everything, rather than in the `spawn` system:
Super Mario Bros.' RunNormalEnemies ends in OffscreenBoundsCheck, so
an enemy goes on the frame its own step takes it past the line.
Since core 0.4.18.

despawn_ahead.description:
Entities other than the player go when their left edge is this many
pixels right of the view's right edge (along y: their top below the
view's bottom). Without it they stay.

despawn_at.description:
What `despawn_behind` and `despawn_ahead` measure from the view's
edges: `edge` (the default), the entity's far edge behind and its
near edge ahead; or `position`, its position's whole pixels both
ways (Super Mario Bros.' OffscreenBoundsCheck compares
Enemy_X_Position). Since core 0.4.10.

despawn_behind.description:
Entities other than the player go when their right edge is this many
pixels left of the view. Without it they stay. Along y (their bottom
edge above the view) when the level's camera follows y only.

draw.description:
The level is drawn ahead of the view in sets of columns, and a
spawn marked `drawn` appears as its column is drawn. Since core
0.4.10.

empty.description:
Feature `level.empty`: a level of `size` empty cells, with no grid
and no layout. A new game's skeleton (`gp game new`) starts with one,
so its model runs and its clips can be scored before the level is
lifted from the game.

exit.description: Ways to other levels besides `next`, for the progression graph.

grid.description:
A slot of kind `level-grid`: the level's tiles. A level has either
a grid or a `layout`.

ground.description:
Feature `level.ground`: the level's ground as one-row boxes read
from runs in two `byte-rows` slots, which a body on the ground
follows by its feet in place of the tile surfaces.

halfway.description:
Feature `level.halfway`: where `restart-level` starts this level again,
rather than the level last started, once the view got far enough
in it (a checkpoint).

hard_spawns.description:
Since 0.4.26: the level's `spawn_objects` list also places the
objects it marks for hard mode, which are left out otherwise.
Super Mario Bros.' ProcessEnemyData skips them until
SecondaryHardMode is set, from level 5-3 on.

hazard.description: What a `hazard` tile does to the player touching it.

hit_widths.description:
The width, in pixels, an entity's touches use in this level in place
of its hitbox's, by entity name, as Super Mario Bros.' SPBBox picks
a narrower box for lifts in castles and hard mode.

ice.description:
Running on `ice` tiles: these replace the entity's acceleration and
deceleration while it stands on one.

kill_below.description:
A player whose top edge is at or below this y has fallen into a pit
and dies.

kind_property.description:
With `grid`: the tileset property whose value `tile_kinds` reads,
instead of solid or not by `solid_property`.

ladder_stops.description:
Feature `level.ladder_stops`: the boxes where a climb is refused,
read as `ladders` is, for a climber's `climb.top_test`. Donkey
Kong's $D50A refuses a climb where Mario's feet box meets one of the
broken ladders' zones ($C161 and $C16E for 25m).

ladder_tops.description:
Feature `level.ladder_tops`: the boxes of the level's ladder tops,
read from two `byte-rows` slots as `ladders` is, for a climber's
`climb.top_test`. Donkey Kong's $D50A tests Mario's feet box against
each stage's list of whole ladders' top rows ($C127 and $C143 for
25m).

ladders.description:
Feature `level.ladders`: the level's ladders as boxes, read from two
`byte-rows` slots, for a climber's `climb.grab`.

layout.description:
An entry of a `level-objects` slot: the objects that build the
level's tiles.

loop_back.description:
With `draw`: places the level tests the player as it is drawn, and
sends them back if they aren't where it wants them.

next.description: The level the `next-level` action goes to.

origin.description:
The level's place in a stage of several levels (rooms), in pixels:
what a state mapping adds to a position in it to compare with a
game that counts positions across the whole stage.

pickups.description:
Feature `level.pickups`: groups of places the player takes by
touching them, read from a byte table, each kept in a counter. A
group may leave a hole where a place was taken (feature
`level.pickup_holes`).

pit_event.description:
Since 0.4.9: a player falling into the pit fires this event (one of
`model.events`) on the frame its top edge first reaches
`kill_below`, instead of dying, and goes on moving, so the model's
rules say what a fall does and when the life ends. Super Mario
Bros.' PlayerHole locks the screen once Mario is below it and ends
the life only later, while he and the enemies go on.

present.description: How the level looks. Presentation only.

respawn.description:
An entity that leaves by `despawn_behind` or `despawn_ahead` waits at
its spawn to appear again when the view comes back within
`spawn_ahead` of it, rather than going for good.

scroll_stop.description:
With `draw`: what drawing one column does. Super Mario Bros.'
ScrollLockObject_Warp, a warp zone's area object.

size.description: Width and height in grid cells.

slot_rest.description:
With `spawn_slots`, the slots are numbered and keep what their last
entity left: an entity that appears takes the lowest free one and
starts with that entity's speed up and down and the fraction of
its place across, as Super Mario Bros.' enemy init routines leave
Enemy_Y_Speed and Enemy_X_MoveForce as the slot had them. A level
starts with them 0. The slots are world state. Since core 0.4.11.

solid_property.description: The tileset property that makes a tile solid. Needed with `grid`.

spawn_ahead.description:
Entities other than the player appear when their spawn's x comes
within this many pixels right of the view (along y, below it, when
the level's camera follows y only). Without it every entity appears
when the level starts.

spawn_in_order.description:
Entities appear by the view in the order of their spawns (the
`drawn` ones aside), at most one for each free slot a frame: one
waits for those before it, and one whose spawn is already left of
the view's last column when its turn comes never appears. Super
Mario Bros.' ProcessEnemyData. Since core 0.4.10.

spawn_objects.description:
An entry of a `spawn-objects` slot: more entities, placed by the
slot's `entities`.

spawn_slots.description:
At most this many entities other than the player (and those with
`no_slot`) are in the level at once: one whose spawn comes within
reach of the view while all are taken waits, and a `drawn` one is
left out. Super Mario Bros.' five enemy slots. Since core 0.4.10.

tile_kinds.description:
The kind of tile each value is: of `kind_property` for a grid, or of
the object format's collision class for a layout (Mega Man 2's
stage classes). Keys are the values in decimal. A value not listed
keeps the kind the format gives it (solid or empty).

tile_size.description: Width and height of a grid cell in pixels.

tile_surfaces.description:
Feature `level.tile_surfaces`: for a tile value, the pixel row
inside its cell where a top-only or ladder tile stands (0 is the
cell's top). A body standing on such tiles follows the surface as
it walks, a pixel at a time (Donkey Kong's sloped girders). Keys are
tile values in decimal, as `tile_kinds`'.

tileset.description:
A slot of kind `metatiles`: what each grid number is. Needed with
`grid`.

water.description:
Falling in `water` tiles: these replace the entity's gravity and
fall limit while its hitbox's middle is in one.

LevelCamera.description: A level's camera settings, for every camera while that level plays.

axis.description: The axes it follows along, instead of the camera's.

hold_player.description:
While it's more than `step` from where it's going, the followed
entity doesn't move: a game that scrolls in steps and holds the
player meanwhile.

keep_in_view.description:
Feature `level.camera.keep_in_view`: the followed entity's bounds
in the view across while this level plays, instead of the camera's
`keep_in_view` and its `keep_in_view_rows`. Donkey Kong's walk
stops at a stage's own edges ($D99D reads them by $53 from $C1B4):
sprite x 16 to 224 on 25m, 8 to 232 on 50m.

keep_in_view_rows.description:
Feature `level.camera.keep_in_view_rows`: with `keep_in_view`, other
bounds while the followed entity's row is in a range, as a camera's
`keep_in_view_rows`. Donkey Kong's $D990 stops a walk left at sprite
x 104 on 75m's fifth girder as on 25m's sixth ($D9C3-$D9DB).

lead.description: The lead, instead of the camera's.

step.description: The most pixels it moves in a frame; without it, it moves at once.

LevelPresent.description:
How a level looks: presentation only, which the simulation never reads
and a theme may replace.

background.description:
The background color: a row of a `table` slot whose first column is
a color number.

cycles.description:
Palette colors that change over time in this level, instead of the
model's `present.cycles`.

effect_order.description:
Feature `present.effect_order`: each effect's place in the same
table, by the event that starts it, so it is painted under or over
the bodies as the console draws it. Donkey Kong's points sprites
are $02C0 and $02C8 ($CFC6), sprites 48 and 50, over the hammers'
52 and under the barrels' 12 on. Presentation only.

label.description: The level's name as the HUD shows it, such as "1-1".

palettes.description:
A slot of kind `palettes`: the level's palettes, background first,
then sprites. Without it the level has the model's.

sprite_order.description:
Feature `present.sprite_order`: each entity's place in the
console's sprite table in this level, by entity name, which the
sprite limit (`present.screen.sprite_limit`) reads: on a line past
the limit the sprites that come last in the table are the ones not
drawn. Entities not named come after those named, in body order.
Presentation only.

Locks.description:
Feature `power.locks`: while `while` holds (a counter compared with a
number, as `invincible`'s), the named actions count as not held and not
pressed for this entity's jump and climb. Donkey Kong's hammer: with
its timer running, A doesn't jump and Up doesn't take a ladder.

actions.description: The actions taken away, by name.

LoopBack.description:
A level that loops: when its draw finishes a check's column with a slot
free, a player who isn't standing at the check's height goes back
`back` pixels with the view and the draw, the level's other entities go
and wait at their spawns (a `drawn` spawn behind the draw never comes
back), and the last `keep` columns drawn go back with the view. Super
Mario Bros.' castle mazes (ProcLoopCommand, ExecGameLoopback).

back.description: Pixels back: a whole number of the draw's steps and of tiles.

keep.description:
Columns behind the draw that go back with the view: the columns the
game's tile buffer holds.

x.description: The column, in pixels, the draw has reached.

y.description: The player's whole pixels down that pass, standing.

Machine.description:
A state machine: the game's (`rules`) or an entity's (`states`). The
current state's first transition whose event fires, or whose time is up,
and whose `if` holds, moves it to another state.

MotionPresent.description:
A move up and down: each frame the place goes by `speed`, then the
speed by `gravity`, at most `max_fall`. Down is positive.

MusicBinding.description:
A song that plays while a level plays, or while a rule state holds (a
state's music takes over from the level's).

song.description: The song's name in the slot's set.

Near.description: How a touch tests points of the player (`contact.near`).

right.description:
An entity this many pixels or more from the view's left edge touches
nothing (FirebarCollision's `cmp #$f0`). Default no limit.

within.description:
A point touches while it is less than this many pixels from the
entity's position on both axes.

Orbit.description:
A pivot that turns an angle and carries parts around it (since 0.4.1).
On its first frame it moves by `place` and spawns `parts` of the entity
`part` where it is. Then each frame (only while its x is inside the view
with `in_view`) its angle moves by `spin` steps of the `angles` in a
