turn (negative: the other way); landing on an angle in `skip` it goes a
step on. The
angle is kept in 256ths of a step in the body's mechanic word 0. A
firebar.

angle_in_slot.description:
In a level with `slot_rest`, a new pivot takes its whole angle from
its slot's speed up and down, wrapped to `angles`, and a pivot that
leaves puts its whole angle there. Super Mario Bros.'
InitShortFirebar clears FirebarSpinState_Low only, and
FirebarSpinState_High is the slot's Enemy_Y_Speed. Default off: it
starts at angle 0.

place_on_appear.description:
Since 0.4.20: it moves by `place` and spawns its parts on the frame
it appears, in the spawn system, rather than on its first turn in
the enemies system, so its first turn already moves its angle.
Super Mario Bros.' InitShortFirebar runs as the area parser puts
the firebar in its slot, and ProcFirebar spins it from the next
frame.

OrbitPart.description:
A part carried by an `orbit` pivot (since 0.4.1): on its first frame it
finds its pivot, the nearest body with an `orbit` within `within`
pixels of where it was placed, and which part it is (the parts placed
there before it). Each frame it's at the pivot plus an offset from a
quarter-turn table: the entity's `ext_tables` `offsets` (one run of
entries per part, a quarter turn and one long), `rows` (where each
part's run starts) and `signs` (each quarter turn's signs, bit 0 for x
and bit 1 for y). x takes the angle folded into a quarter turn and y the
angle a quarter turn on. It leaves when its pivot does.

Oscillate.description:
Swinging around a center on one axis (since 0.4.1): each frame its
speed along the axis moves by `force` toward the center, up to
`max_speed` either way, and it moves by its speed, through tiles. The
center is `center` pixels from where it's placed, or `low_center` when
it's placed at or past `low_at` along the axis. A flying enemy that bobs
around a point, or a lift that swings.

move_first.description:
Since 0.4.23: it moves by the speed it had before the force is
added, which is chosen by where it was before the move.

rest_creep_every.description:
At no speed along the axis, its position's fraction is cleared, and
short of where it's placed it takes no force and moves a pixel
toward that place on frames that are multiples of this number
(Super Mario Bros.' ProcMoveRedPTroopa).

starts_at_rest.description:
Since 0.4.23: it starts with no speed, whatever its numbered slot's
last body left there (`slot_rest`).

PaletteRef.description: One palette of a `palettes` slot, by number from 0.

Path.description:
Moving back and forth along one axis from the spawn: out by `distance`
(negative: left or up) at `speed`, waiting `pause` frames at each end,
and back. With `wait_near`, it doesn't leave the spawn end while the
player's x is within that many pixels of its own. With `every` (since
0.4.7), it moves only on frames whose number plus `phase` is a multiple
of `every`. No gravity, through tiles.

every.description:
Since 0.4.7: it moves only on frames whose number plus `phase` is a
multiple of this (Super Mario Bros.' piranha plant moves a pixel on
odd frames). 0 or 1 for every frame.

speed.description: Pixels per frame, without its sign.

wait_near_wrap.description:
Since 0.4.10, with `wait_near`: the distance across, in whole
pixels, is taken modulo this before it is compared, as Super Mario
Bros.' ChkPlayerNearPipe compares only PlayerEnemyDiff's low byte
(256), so a plant a page and a few pixels from Mario waits. 0 for
none.

Patrol.description:
Walking back and forth between the spawn's `x` and its `patrol_end`
parameter, turning at each end.

period.description: It moves once every this many frames.

step.description: Pixels moved each time it moves.

Pickup.description:
Pickup points (since 0.4.18). After the frame's moves, while the entity
meets tiles, the first point in a cell of kind `tile` turns the cell
into `becomes` and fires `event` for the entity. It takes one cell a
frame, and the wall points aren't tested on that frame.

event.description:
An event fired for the entity: the core's, an extension's or the
model's own.

points.description:
The points, x and y from the entity's position, in whole pixels,
tested in order.

PickupCells.description:
Feature `level.pickup_cells`: place k's first cell is the number made
of the bytes at `at[0] + k` (high) and `at[1] + k` (low) of the group's
`table`, less `base`, counted row by row across the level's width; it
covers `size` cells across and down from there, less any outside the
level. Donkey Kong's $EF38
writes blank tiles ($24) over a rivet taken (1 by 1, as $CC = $11 at
$EEB6 asks) or a prize (2 by 2, $CC = $22 at $EF0C), at the name-table
address $C5D6 (high) and $C5E9 (low) give the place's entry.

at.description: The indexes in `table` of the first place's high and low byte.

base.description: The number of the level's first cell.

Pickups.description:
Feature `level.pickups`: `count` places, their x from index `x_at` of
the byte table `table` (a slot's column, `slot.column`) on and their y
from `y_at` on. Place k is in the counter `<counter>_<k>`, 0 while it
is there and 1 once taken; the level's counters set them at its start.
After the player's moves, on a frame it moved across or is in a jump,
its place less `offset` touches the first place not taken whose x is
its x and whose y is within `window` of its y (place y + window[0] to
place y + window[1], edges included), unless it is falling off a ledge
or out: the place's counter becomes 1 and `event` fires. Groups are
tested in order and one touch a frame ends the test. Donkey Kong's
$EE79 tests Mario's sprite ($0200, $0203: his place less 5) against
100m's 8 rivets ($C5AE and $C5C2 from entry 11, a window of 16 above)
and then the stage's 3 prizes ($EEF0, entry $C5FA[$53], exact), on a
frame his step beat $BE is set, and returns after the first it finds.

by_hook.description:
Feature `level.pickup_by_hook`: the engine takes none of the
group's places; an `ext` hook sets its counters, and the group gives
the places' cells (`level.pickup_cells`). Original Edition's 50m
takes a prize on a climb's step too ($EEF0 on $BE), which the
`dk_prizes` hook models, and $EF38 blanks its cells as on 100m.

cells.description:
Feature `level.pickup_cells`: the level's cells a place covers,
which show an empty cell's picture (`present.cells`, kind `empty`)
once it is taken. Presentation only: the cells' kinds stay.

counter.description: The counters' name: place k's is `<counter>_<k>`.

event.description: An event (one of `model.events`) fired on a take.

hole.description:
Feature `level.pickup_holes`: a place taken is a hole, this box
(left, top, right, bottom from the place, edges included): a touch
of it, as a take's but not in a jump, starts the player's fall off
a ledge (`jump.ledge_fall`) on the next frame, and that fall doesn't
land on a ground box (`level.ground`) on the hole's rows while the
player's feet are within the hole. Donkey Kong's $EED9 puts Mario in
his fall ($96 = 8) on a removed rivet's spot unless he is jumping;
the fall ($D697) goes 2 pixels a frame down past the floor, whose
box test ($D2CB) finds no floor under him there.

offset.description:
What the player's place less this is compared with: Donkey Kong's
sprite is 5 left of and above Mario's place.

window.description:
The y window from a place's y, low and high, edges included; [0, 0]
for the same y.

x_at.description: The index in `table` of the first place's x.

y_at.description: The index in `table` of the first place's y.

Present.description:
How the game is shown. Presentation only: the simulation never reads
it, and a theme may replace any of it.

cells.description:
The feature `present.cells`: how a cell the game changes is drawn (a coin
taken, a block used), and a held cell's bump.

cycles.description:
Palette colors that change over time in every level whose `present`
doesn't give its own.

effects.description:
The feature `present.effects`: short-lived pictures the model's events start,
such as a coin popping out of a block.

hidden.description:
Feature `present.hidden`: bodies the game doesn't draw while a
rule state holds and counters are in ranges, though they are
still in play, such as Donkey Kong's sprites from a death's 13th
divider wrap ($F08C) until the 21st draws the stage's objects
again ($CC34).

hud.description: The heads-up display drawn over the view, such as a status bar.

screen.description:
The picture the game puts out: its size, its pixels' shape and the
edges a television hides.

screens.description:
Feature `present.screens`: whole screens shown in place of the
level, its bodies and the HUD while a rule state holds, such as a
title and its menu.

sound.description:
What plays: music by level and by rule state, sound effects by
event. Since core 0.4.3.

Ratio.description: A positive ratio of whole numbers: "N" or "N/D".

Ref.description:
One piece of support. `at` is `path:line` for a file in the repo, which
`gp model check` checks, or any other reference (a recording ID).

in.description:
A pinned download the file is in rather than the repo, as
`<name>@<revision>`, such as `smbdis@7e8e9777`: `at` is then a path
within it.

Replaced.description:
How a body draws the picture of the body it replaced. Presentation
only.

flip_y.description: The picture mirrored top to bottom.

Ride.description: How the player rides an entity it stands on (`contact.ride`).

above.description: A box whose top is above this y isn't tested (`cmp #$20`). Default 0.

copy_below.description:
A second box this many pixels below the first, tested after it.
Super Mario Bros.' SmallPlatformCollision moves the box down $80 and
tests again. Default 0: one box.

wrap.description:
The boxes' heights wrap at this y, as the game's height byte does.
Default 0: no wrap.

RowRef.description: One row of a lifted table, by number from 0.

Run.description: Moving left and right with the input actions `left` and `right`.

acceleration.description:
Speed gained per frame toward the top speed. Without it the top
speed is reached at once.

air_control.description: Can change direction and speed in the air, as on the ground.

air_run_from.description:
Since 0.4.3, with `run_speed` and `air_control`: in the air the run
counts (its top speed and `run_acceleration`) while the speed as the
frame starts (whole steps with `move_step`, without its sign) is at
least this, and doesn't count below it, whatever the run action and
its hold.

air_speed.description:
The top speed in the air while a direction is held, instead of
`walk_speed`, with `air_control`.

air_step_cycle.description:
Feature `run.air_step_cycle`, with `step_cycle` and without
`air_control`: in the air the entity moves across by this list
instead of its speed, the way it took off (the way held on the
takeoff frame; none held, it doesn't move across), by a counter of
its own in mechanic word 1, which a frame that moves advances first.
Donkey Kong's jump moves Mario a pixel every other frame by the
toggle $9E: `[1, 0]`.

both_left.description:
Feature `run.both_left`: left and right held together turn the
entity left and move it nowhere, on the ground and (with
`climb.lone_way`) on a ladder. Donkey Kong's pad routine $D175
writes $57 left for the pad's Left and Right bits together and
leaves $56 0, so Mario faces left and stands (wallW's pad probes,
2026-11-04: x kept at 120 on girder 1 with both held).

cap_whole.description:
Since 0.4.2, with `move_step` and `acceleration`: a direction held
adds its rate whatever the speed, and the top speed then caps the
whole steps only, keeping the fraction, so the speed wobbles just
above the top speed (just below it going left).

decel_bands.description:
Since 0.4.2: while the run doesn't count, at or above a band's
`from` speed its `rate` replaces the walking rates (`acceleration`,
`deceleration` and `skid_deceleration`): slowing down faster from a
high speed. In order of `from`.

decel_hold_from.description:
Since 0.4.2, with `decel_bands`: once the speed reaches this on the
ground, the last band's rate holds, whatever the speed, until a
direction is held the way it last moved on the ground while the
speed is below this. A frame that jumps changes neither.

deceleration.description:
Speed lost per frame with no direction held. Without it the entity
stops at once.

face_both.description:
Since 0.4.15: both directions held where the facing turns face the
entity neither way, and count as a way of their own for the run's
tests against the way it last moved, though right still wins for
the speed. A `skid_by = "last_motion"` then doubles the rate on the
next frame whichever way it moved, and a slow skid leaves it last
moved both ways. Super Mario Bros.' OnGroundStateSub stores
Left_Right_Buttons in PlayerFacingDir as it is, 3 with both held,
which X_Physics compares with Player_MovingDir. It is world state
(`facing` and `moved` are `both`).

face_on_ground.description:
Since 0.4.3: the facing changes only on the ground. In the air a
direction held still moves the speed, but the entity keeps the way
it faced, so with `skid_by = "last_motion"` pressing back in the air
doesn't double the rate.

face_way.description:
Feature `run.face_way`: the facing is a way the game keeps from
the pad: the frame a jump takes off (with `takeoff_in_air`) turns
the entity to a lone direction held, a landing hold (`jump.land_hold`)
keeps it, a turn at the view's edge in the air
(`camera.keep_in_view_turn`) turns it with the speed, and a level's
restart keeps it. Donkey Kong's pad routine $D175 writes $57 from
Left or Right held alone on every frame but the jump's and the
walk-off fall's ($CEC1-$CED3), the jump's edge turn writes it
($D55F-$D56E), the stage setup leaves it, and $F070 mirrors his
pictures by it.

lone_direction.description:
Feature `run.lone_direction`: left or right moves the entity only
held alone, with neither of its climb's up and down actions held.
Donkey Kong's walk and hammer routines move Mario only while the
pad's latched byte $56 is exactly 1 or 2 ($D1CF, $D6DE), so Up or
Down with a direction stands him still.

move_step.description:
Since 0.4.2: the entity moves by its speed rounded down to a
multiple of this step, and the rest of the speed is kept apart and
carried to the next frame's speed (the state's `vx` is the whole
steps and `vx_frac` the rest). With nothing held, `deceleration`
slows it only while its whole steps aren't 0, so a stop keeps the
rest. Speeds compared with `skid_turn_below` and the bands are the
whole steps.

off.description:
Since 0.4.16: the run does nothing, so the speed across stays as it
is and no input reaches it. For a machine state to set: while
Super Mario Bros.' PlayerDeath runs, PlayerCtrlRoutine loads no
buttons and GameEngine clears Left_Right_Buttons every frame, so
ImposeFriction doesn't run.

push_masks.description:
Since 0.4.8: on the frame after a wall or the feet push the entity
out to one side, a direction held toward that side doesn't change
its speed, as if nothing were held, as Super Mario Bros.'
ImpedePlayerMove clears that side's bit of Player_CollisionBits and
ImposeFriction masks the buttons with it the next frame. The side is
world state (`pushed`).

run_hold_frames.description:
Since 0.4.2, with `run_speed`: each frame the run action counts on
the ground (not a frame that jumps) sets a count to this, and the
count goes down by one as each frame starts; while it is above 0
the run still counts. So the run is kept
for this many frames, less one, after the action is let go.

run_with_motion.description:
Since 0.4.2, with `run_speed`: the run action (and its hold) counts
only while the direction held is the way the entity last moved, or
while nothing is held before it has moved at all. A run pressed with
a direction from a level start, or while skidding, walks first.

skid_by.description:
Since 0.4.2: what makes a skid. `speed` (the default): a direction
held against the speed, on the ground, slows by
`skid_deceleration`. `last_motion`: the rate in use (any of them)
doubles while the entity faces away from the way it last moved,
so its first step after a level start, when it hasn't moved yet,
is doubled too. The facing is the one the frame starts with.

skid_deceleration.description:
Speed lost per frame while the direction held is against the
entity's motion, on the ground: a skid. Without it a turn uses
`acceleration`.

skid_turn_below.description:
Since 0.4.2: on the ground (not on a frame that jumps), a direction
held against the way it last moved, while the speed is below this,
sets the speed to 0 at once and turns; the frame's rate then applies
the new way.

skid_turn_with.description:
Since 0.4.11, with `skid_turn_below`: input actions that steer for
the quick turn as a direction does. While one of them is held and
no direction is, or a direction that isn't the way it last moved,
a speed below `skid_turn_below` is set to 0 at once and the entity
turns to the way it faces, on the ground and not on a frame that
jumps. Super Mario Bros.' GetPlayerAnimSpeed takes any button but A
as steering (ChkSkid), so B held after letting go of the direction
stops Mario dead below $0b.

speed_before_walls.description:
Since 0.4.11: the run's speed tests (`decel_bands`,
`decel_hold_from`, `skid_turn_below`, `air_run_from`) and the jump's
`bands` read the speed as the run itself last left it, before a
wall stopped it, instead of the speed as the frame starts. The run
leaves it each frame on the ground, and in the air while a
direction is held. Super Mario Bros.' ImposeFriction writes
Player_XSpeedAbsolute and ImpedePlayerMove nulls Player_X_Speed
only, so the frame after Mario runs into a wall still reads his
running speed. It is world state (`seen_speed`).

start.description:
The first steps from standing: `frames` frames at `speed` before
the speed moves toward the top speed as usual.

step_cycle.description:
Feature `run.step_cycle`: the whole pixels the entity moves on each
walking frame on the ground, by a step counter it keeps in its
mechanic word 0. A walking frame (a direction held, on the ground)
first advances the counter by one, back to 0 at the list's length,
then moves the entry at the counter, and `walk_speed` no longer
moves it. The counter also advances on every frame in the air and
of a `jump.land_hold`, and not while it stands. Donkey Kong's walk
routine steps one counter, $88, through 15 frames, moving on the
bits of the pattern $DB/$36: 2 px every 3 frames, the same both
ways, with the phase kept through stops and jumps.

takeoff_in_air.description:
Since 0.4.3, with `jump`: the frame a jump starts from the ground is
a frame in the air for the run, as in a game that sets the jump
state before it moves the player across. With nothing held the
speed is kept, and a direction held uses the air's rules
(`air_run_from` included) and doesn't slow the first steps.

wall_snap.description:
Holding a direction into a wall the tile hitbox touches clears the
position's fraction, as a game that pushes its player back to the
wall's edge each frame does.

walls.description:
Since 0.4.5: walls are found at points instead of across the tile
hitbox, after the vertical move. The move across doesn't stop at a
tile; once the frame's moves are done, the first of the points (left
ones first) in a cell that stops movement pushes the entity one
pixel away from it and stops its speed across, unless it moves away
from that side. A machine state's `set` can change them.

Screen.description: The screen a game draws to.

overscan.description:
Pixels hidden at the left, top, right and bottom edges, as a
television's frame hides them. Default none.

pixel_aspect.description:
A pixel's width over its height on the display the game was made
for ("8/7" for the NTSC NES). Default "1".

size.description:
Width and height in pixels, as the console puts them out (256 by
240 for the NES).

sprite_limit.description:
Since core 0.4.14: the console draws at most this many sprites on
a line, and the game's own sprites past it drop out or flicker.
Presentation only; a player can turn it off.

sprite_x_wraps.description:
The console's sprite x is a byte, so a sprite the game places left
of the screen (x below 0) shows at x + 256, at the right edge: each
hardware sprite of a body's picture (8 pixels across) whose left
column is left of the screen is drawn 256 pixels on. Donkey Kong's
hammer swung left of Mario at the screen's left edge puts its head
at x 255 ($02D3 wraps). Presentation only, for a game that never
scrolls. Feature `present.sprite_x_wraps`.

sprites_off.description:
Rule states, each `<machine>.<state>`, in which the console's
sprite layer is off: the level, the HUD's tiles and the bodies
drawn as name-table tiles show, and no sprite does. Donkey Kong
turns its sprites off once a Start pause's 64 frames are out
($CFA1 sets bit 4 of $11, which the NMI writes to $2001 inverted).
Presentation only. Feature `present.sprites_off`.

at.description: The tile's top left corner, in screen pixels, with the counter at 0.

counter.description: A counter that moves it: `step` pixels for each 1 of its value.

step.description: Pixels across and down for each 1 of the counter.

tile.description: The tile's number in that slot.

tiles.description: A slot of kind `tiles`: the sprite tiles.

ScreenText.description: A line of text on a [`StateScreen`], written into its name table.

at.description: The first character's tile column and row.

palette.description:
The background palette its cells are drawn in, 0 to 3, in place
of the attribute bytes'. Default 0.

text.description: The characters, each one of the HUD font's.

ScrollStop.description: A level's column that stops the scroll when it is drawn.

at.description:
Where the column is along the level's axis, in pixels. From the
frame after it is drawn no camera moves in this level.

removes.description:
Entities of these kinds in the level as the column is drawn go,
with no event (KillEnemies clears the enemy slots holding one).

SfxBinding.description: An effect played when an event fires.

effect.description: The effect's name in the slot's set.

Shoot.description:
Spawning another entity: when `action` is pressed, or every `every`
frames, while fewer than `max` of it are in the level. It appears
`ahead` from this entity's position, x mirrored when this one faces
left, facing the same way. One of `action` and `every`.

after_move.description:
Since 0.4.10, a player's: it shoots after it moves this frame, from
where it has got to, as Super Mario Bros.' ProcFireball_Bubble runs
in GameEngine after GameRoutines has moved Mario.

in_slots.description:
Since 0.4.12: the `max` shots take numbered slots in turn, nothing
is shot while the slot whose turn it is holds one, and a new shot
sets only the whole parts of its place and speed down, keeping the
fractions its slot's last shot left. FireballObjCore never clears
SprObject_YMF_Dummy or SprObject_Y_MoveForce, and
ProcFireball_Bubble picks the slot by FireballCounter's low bit.

unmirrored.description:
Since 0.4.10: `ahead` across isn't mirrored for a shooter facing
left (Super Mario Bros.' fireball starts 4 pixels right of Mario
whichever way he faces).

vx.description:
Since 0.4.10: the new body's speed across, mirrored for a shooter
facing left (a fireball's $40 or $c0, 4 pixels a frame).

vx_both.description:
The new body's speed across, signed and not mirrored, for a shooter
facing both ways (`run.face_both`). FireballObjCore indexes
FireballXSpdData by PlayerFacingDir less 1, so a facing of 3 reads
the byte after the table, the routine's own first opcode, $86: 8
pixels left less $60 sixteenths of the next pixel, -7.625 a frame.

vy.description:
Since 0.4.10: the new body's speed up and down (a fireball starts
falling at 4).

whole.description:
Since 0.4.10: the new body starts from the shooter's place in whole
pixels, its fractions 0 (FireballObjCore copies Player_X_Position
and Player_Y_Position, not their fractions).

Shuttle.description:
Moving back and forth by a counter (since 0.4.1): on frames whose
number is a multiple of `every`, it counts a move, turns once the count
passes `turn_after` (and counts from 0 again), and moves `step` pixels
along `axis` the way it's going, right or down first, through tiles.
With `sway`, each move also goes `sway.step` across the other axis,
toward the far side while the frame number divided by `sway.half` is
odd and back otherwise: a flier that bobs as it goes. The count and the
way are the body's mechanic words 0 and 1, so it has no `ext` hook.

Sides.description:
Where a touch counts as a side of the entity (`contact.sides`, since
0.4.22), in pixels, measured with the touch's edges.

left.description:
The player is on the left side while its right edge is less than
this past the entity's left edge.

right.description:
The player is on the right side while its left edge is less than
this before the entity's right edge.

top.description:
A falling player whose bottom edge is less than this past the
entity's top edge isn't at a side.

oneOf.description: A direction held against the speed, on the ground.
Facing away from the way it last moved: the rate in use doubles.

Sound.description:
Music and sound effects, bound to the model. Presentation only: no
state hash depends on them, and a theme may restyle them by the `sound`
role group.

music.description: Songs and the levels or rule states they play in.

roles.description:
Feature `present.sound_roles`: the game's sound requests named as
sound roles, each cued by a counter that holds the request. A theme
replaces a role's sound with a file (docs/formats/theme.md, "Sound
replacements"), played on the role's cue in place of what the
model's own sound plays.

sfx.description: Effects and the events they mark.

silent_while.description:
Feature `present.sound_silent_while`: counter tests while any of
which the game makes no sound, though it asks for some (an attract
demo that sets its tune's request with the sound channels off). A
theme's sound per role is silent then too.

SoundCapture.description: Where a sound slot's songs are captured from.

frames.description: Its frames, as `gp sound capture --frames` takes them (`A..B`).

name.description: The capture's name, which its files are kept under.

recording.description: The recording's ID (or a unique prefix of it).

SoundRole.description:
A sound role (feature `present.sound_roles`): a request the game makes,
named, with the counter test that marks it. The cue reads the world
after a tick, as every other presentation does.

counter.description: The counter that holds the request.

description.description:
When it plays, in plain words and without any character's name: a
theme maker's prompt starts from it.

equals.description:
The masked counter equals this for the cue (default: any value but
0).

frames.description: Its usual length in frames, as a theme maker's guide.

held.description:
The request stays set while the sound plays (a held tune): the cue
starts the role on the first frame the test holds and stops it on
the first that it doesn't. Otherwise the game clears the request
each frame, and every frame the test holds starts the role again.

loops.description:
The sound repeats until another music role starts or a held role
stops.

mask.description: The bits of the counter tested (default every bit).

name.description: The role's name: lowercase letters, digits and `_`, such as `jump`.

SoundTest.description: A counter test for the sound (feature `present.sound_silent_while`).

equals.description: The masked counter equals this (default: any value but 0).

oneOf.description: Measured by the pipeline from recordings.
Proposed by an agent.
Said by a person, in words or in the game's own source.

Spawn.description:
Entities placed in a level: one at `x` and `y`, or one per row of a
table slot, with `columns` naming the column each field is read from.

appear_moving.description:
With the level's `appear_still`, it moves on the frame it appears
all the same: a group's members after the first, which
HandleGroupEnemies puts in slots the enemy loop runs later in the
same frame. Since core 0.4.11.

at_edge.description:
When it appears it is placed this many pixels past the view's last
column along the level's axis, instead of at its x (or y), which is
then only where the view reaches it: Super Mario Bros.' group
enemies, which HandleGroupEnemies starts at the screen's right edge
and 24 pixels apart. Since core 0.4.11.

columns.description:
Field name to the table column it's read from (`x`, `y`, or a
parameter).

drawn.description:
It appears when the level's `draw` draws the column its x is in,
rather than by `spawn_ahead`, and only if a slot is free then:
Super Mario Bros.' piranha plants, which VerticalPipe makes as it
draws the pipe's first column. Since core 0.4.10.

params.description: Per-entity parameters extensions define, such as `patrol_end`.

table.description: A slot of kind `table`, one entity per row.

SpeedStep.description: Frames per picture at and above a speed.

Split.description:
A sprite's `split` (feature `sprite.split`): the part `keep` (left,
top, width and height in pixels from the picture's top left as drawn,
after any flip) stays where the body's picture is, and the rest of the
picture is drawn moved by `x` and `y`, counters' values (0 without
one). The kept part is drawn over the rest, as a console draws its
first sprites over later ones. While both values are 0 the picture is
drawn whole as usual.

SpringBoost.description:
A higher throw: from step `from_step` (counted from 0) on, `action`
newly pressed (or held, with `held`) on any frame of the press makes
the throw `speed` instead.

SpringStep.description: One step of a springboard's press.

move.description: The player's move each frame, in pixels (positive down).

offset.description: The springboard's place below where it was placed, in pixels.

Springboard.description:
A springboard (since 0.4.4): a player that stands on it (its feet on
the springboard's top as placed, or riding it through `contact.stand`)
is held for the frames of its `steps`, then thrown up at `speed`. Each
frame of a step moves the player by the step's `move` (positive down)
and puts the springboard at its `offset` below where it was placed.
While held the player doesn't move by its speed, jump or fall, though
its run still changes its speed. The press's last frame throws it,
higher with a `boost`. With `throw_late` the thrown player stands one
more frame, moving across but not up, and rises from the frame after,
as when a game throws after the player's move. The press is kept in
the body's mechanic words 0 to 2, so a springboard has no `ext` hook.
Its `on_ground` is false while it presses, for its sprite's clips.
Super Mario Bros.' jumpspring, or any spring or trampoline.

speed.description: The vertical speed of a plain throw (negative, up).

Sprite.description: How an entity is drawn. Presentation only.

behind.description:
Drawn behind the level's picture: its pixels show only where the
level draws its backdrop, as the NES's sprite priority bit does. A
plant in a pipe. A state's `set` can turn it on and off. Since core
0.4.18.

behind_when.description:
Drawn behind the level's picture, as `behind`, on the frames this
holds: a game that sets a sprite's priority bit by where the object
is or what it is doing, as Donkey Kong gives a barrel rolling on
the bottom girder left of x $30 attribute $23, behind the oil drum
($DFC3). Presentation only. Feature `sprite.behind_when`.

blink.description:
Hidden on every other run of `every` frames while `when` holds,
whatever it shows otherwise: a hurt entity's blink. Counted by the
game's frames. Since core 0.4.2.

cells.description:
Each tile's own flips and palette, in the order of the tiles: the
sprite as a layout of tiles, as a console's sprite attribute bytes
give it. A game that saves tiles by mirroring half a sprite says so
here. Without it every tile is drawn as it is, in `palette`.

clips.description:
Animation: the first clip whose `when` holds is drawn; when none
does, the frame above is.

colors.description:
Colors of its own for `palette`: one palette of a `palettes` slot,
such as a power-up's colors.

copy.description:
Since core 0.4.20: a second picture below the first (Super Mario Bros.'
DrawSmallPlatform draws a small lift twice).

flip_in_place.description:
Mirrored where it is, as a console flips a sprite by its attribute
bits: a facing or clip flip leaves the picture's left edge at
`offset` instead of turning it about the middle of the hitbox.
Donkey Kong draws Mario facing left at the same $0203 as facing
right. Feature `sprite.flip_in_place`.

flip_when_facing_left.description: Mirrored left to right while the entity faces left.

frame.description:
The tile numbers from a lifted table instead: a row of a `rows`
slot, such as one of the game's sprite frames.

front.description:
Drawn over every body without it, whatever their order: a console
draws its first sprites over the rest, and Super Mario Bros. puts
Mario's first (Player_SprDataOffset, DefaultSprOffsets' $04).
Since core 0.4.21.

leaves.description:
The picture a body that replaces this one draws, when its sprite
has `replaced`, in place of this one's last picture turned over: a
game that draws a defeated enemy with a frame of its own, as Super
Mario Bros.' koopas fall as an upside-down shell
(CheckUpsideDownShell). Its slot, frame, width, palette, cells and
offset are read. Since core 0.4.21.

name_table.description:
Tiles the game writes into the background's name table rather
than sprites, drawn as a body: Donkey Kong is background tiles, his
poses rewritten in place. The screen measure counts its pixels as
the background's, and the sprite limit doesn't count it. Feature
`sprite.name_table`.

offset.description:
The picture's top left in pixels from the entity's position, in
place of standing it on the entity's bottom edge; mirrored about
the middle of the hitbox when it faces left, as a sprite-set frame
is. A console that shows a sprite a line below where its table puts
it (the NES) is drawn at `[0, 1]`. Since core 0.4.18.

palette.description: Which palette of the game's palettes the tiles use.

replaced.description:
Drawn as the picture the body it replaced showed last: a body a
defeat leaves (`health.defeat.becomes`) looks like the enemy it
was, turned over with `flip_y`, as Super Mario Bros.' defeated
enemies fall upside down. A body with nothing to copy (one a start
carried in) draws the sprite's own frame. Since core 0.4.21.

split.description:
A part of the picture held where the body is while the rest is
drawn moved by two counters' values: a game that moves one of an
object's hardware sprites and leaves the others where its last
draw put them for a frame, as Donkey Kong moves only Mario's first
sprite on the frame he walks off a girder's end with the hammer
($D70A/$D710, $D72B) and draws none of the others. Presentation
only. Feature `sprite.split`.

tiles.description: Tile numbers, row by row. Give these or `frame`.

SpriteCopy.description: A sprite's second picture (`copy`), in pixels. Presentation only.

above.description: Neither picture shows with its top above this y.

below.description: How far below the first it is.

wrap.description: Its height wraps at this y.

SpriteLimit.description: How many sprites the console draws on one line (core 0.4.14).

flicker.description:
The game turns its sprites' order each frame, so the ones past the
limit take turns and flicker (default false: the same ones drop).

per_line.description: Hardware sprites a line holds (8 on the NES).

sprite_width.description: A hardware sprite's width in pixels (default 8).

SpriteOrder.description:
Feature `present.sprite_order`: body k of an entity takes the table's
sprites from `at + step * k`, k being its slot (its `ext` word `word`
less one, for a hook that keeps the slot there, when set; else the
level's numbered spawn slot it is in) or else its count among the
entity's drawn bodies before it. Donkey Kong's 25m keeps Mario at 0,
the fires from 4, the barrels from 12 ($0230 + 16 * X), the hammers
at 52, the drum's flame at 56 and Pauline at 58. Original Edition's 50m
lays its table out as Mario 0, the fires from 4 ($0210, 16 bytes a
slot, $EFE7), the pies from 12 ($0230 + 16 * $5D, $EFD5), the moving
ladders from 48 ($02C0 + 16 * X, $8899) and the hammers at 60.

at.description: The first hardware sprite's number in the table (0 to 63).

turn.description:
The game copies the slots into the table starting from a slot that
turns: k is the slot less this counter's value, around `count`
slots. Original Edition's 50m copies its seven pie slots from
$0493, one further each frame ($895F), so the pie a crowded line
drops takes turns.

word.description: The `ext` word that holds the body's slot plus one.

SpriteTurn.description:
Feature `present.sprite_order`: the counter whose value is the first
slot copied, and the slots' count.

Stages.description:
Feature `stages`: the original's stages in order, each played by the
level of its name or, for a stage the model doesn't hold yet, by a
stand-in level. A counter the model's rules step as the game does says
which stage is being played; `next-level` and `restart-level` start the
level that plays it. Donkey Kong's NES port plays 25m, 75m and 100m and
then 25m again a loop harder ($D096-$D0AE); a model with 25m only plays
25m in each slot, while the stage counter, the loops and what they
change (the bonus, the difficulty, the level number) go on as the
game's.

counter.description:
The counter holding the index in `order` of the stage being
played, 0 the first. The model's rules step it, as the game steps
its own stage number.

order.description:
The stages in the order the game plays them: each a level's name,
or the name of a stage the model has no level for yet.

skip.description:
Feature `stages.skip`: stages of `order` the game passes over.
When the rules step the counter onto one, it steps on again the
same way (past the end with its wrap), so no level plays it.
Donkey Kong (JU) has no 50m and steps its stage number $53 from 1
(25m) to 3 (75m); Original Edition's model, loaded with a JU ROM,
skips 50m's place rather than playing a stand-in in it.

stand_in.description: The level that plays a stage of `order` the model has no level for.

enter_keeps_fraction.description:
Since core 0.4.15, with `enter_speed`: the speed up and down keeps
the fraction below a pixel it had, and only its whole pixels are
set. KillPlayer stores Player_Y_Speed and leaves Player_Y_MoveForce
as it was, so Mario's speed is -4 plus the fraction of his last.

enter_speed.description:
Since core 0.4.15, an entity's state only: entering it sets the
entity's speed across and up and down. Super Mario Bros.'
KillPlayer stops Mario across and sets his vertical speed to -4.

frees_at_once.description:
Feature `state.frees_at_once`, a game machine's state: systems that
move things which run for the rest of the frame on which the state
is left, from the system after the one that left it, though the
frame began frozen in it. Donkey Kong's unpause clears $0516 in the
Start check and then counts the frame timers on that frame.

freeze.description:
Nothing in the world moves on a frame that starts with the game, or
any entity, in this state: entering it stops the world from the
next frame, and leaving it starts it again from the next frame.
State machines and timers still run.

ground.description:
Since core 0.4.13, an entity's state only: what entering it does to
the entity's standing. `leave` takes it off the ground, as Super
Mario Bros.' ForceInjury sets Player_State to 1 though Mario stays
where he is; `land` puts it back on the ground if there is ground
under it, as PlayerBGCollision does on the first frame
PlayerCtrlRoutine runs again, though PlayerMovementSubs doesn't move
him while he shrinks.

holds.description:
Since core 0.4.12: counters whose `every` changes wait while the
world starts a frame in this state: the frames still count, up to
the change, and the change is made on the first frame after the
state that comes round to it. Super Mario Bros.' RunGameTimer leaves
while Mario is below the screen, though DecTimers goes on counting
GameTimerCtrlTimer down to 0.

keep_time.description:
Since core 0.4.12: entering this state keeps the frames counted in
the state before, so its `after` counts from when the earlier state
was entered. A run of states that time one span, such as the parts
of a pause, says each part's end from the span's start.

seen_every.description:
Since core 0.4.12, an entity's state only: while a camera `by_move`
follows the entity in this state, it keeps the entity's place in
its view only on frames whose number is a multiple of this, the
frames the entity is drawn. Super Mario Bros.' PlayerGfxHandler
leaves on odd frames while InjuryTimer is set (the blink), before
RenderPlayerSub sets Player_Pos_ForScroll, which ScrollHandler reads.

set.description:
An entity's state only: the entity's fields while in this state,
written as the entity's own are (`hitbox = { ... }`,
`walk = { speed = 2 }`). Tables merge into the entity's, key by key,
and other values replace its.

step_word.description:
Feature `state.step_word`, an entity's state only: on each frame
the entity is in it, frozen or not, its mechanic word 0 (the step
counter of `run.step_cycle`) goes up by one, back to 0 at this, before
its transitions are tested. Donkey Kong's death spin calls $D9E6
every frame, so $88 goes on counting while the world stands still.

stops.description:
Since core 0.4.12: a part freeze. These systems (names from
`model.systems` that move things) don't run on a frame that starts
in this state, from the next frame as with `freeze`, while the
others do. Super Mario Bros.' injury: TimerControl stops the enemies
and the frame timers while the player routine runs on its own
schedule. With `freeze` it is ignored.

stops_at_once.description:
Since core 0.4.12: of the systems this state stops (all that move,
with `freeze`), these also stop for the rest of the frame it is
entered in, when they haven't run yet: InjurePlayer sets
TimerControl inside the enemy loop, so the enemy that hurt Mario
and the ones after it don't move that frame.

stops_machines.description:
Feature `state.stops_machines`: while a frame begins in this state,
the entities' own machines don't run (their time, their
transitions and a `step_word`), as the game machines still do.
Donkey Kong's Start pause stops Mario's routine, his death spin's
counter included, and only the Start check runs.

StateScreen.description:
A screen shown in place of the level while a rule state holds
(feature `present.screens`): its picture, drawn from update strings as
the game writes its name table and palettes, and sprites fixed on it,
each moved by a counter. Donkey Kong's title is the string the title
routine draws ($C807 with 8) and a cursor sprite 16 lines down a menu
line.

blank.description:
The screen is the first level's backdrop color alone, as a console
shows with its picture turned off, in place of a layout (feature
`present.screens_blank`).

from_line.description:
With `blank`: the screen line the picture goes off at (feature
`present.screens_from_line`). The lines above it show the frame as
it would be drawn without this screen, the level, its bodies and
the HUD, and the lines from it the backdrop, as a console whose
picture is turned off partway down the frame. Donkey Kong's stage
clear turns it off at line 34 ($CBB7 -> $D19A on the clear script's
$7A step), so the status rows show on that frame.

layout.description:
An entry of a `screen-text` (update strings) slot: the screen's
name table, attributes and palettes as the game writes them. The
palettes it doesn't write are the first level's. A screen gives it
or `blank`.

states.description: The rule states it shows in, as `<machine>.<state>`.

text.description:
Text written into its name table over the layout or the blank
(feature `present.screens_text`), in the characters of the HUD's
font (`present.hud.font`): Donkey Kong's turn screen, PLAYER I or
PLAYER II on a cleared name table ($CBCA, $C6AA).

when.description:
The model's counters in ranges, each of which must hold too
(feature `present.screens_when`): Donkey Kong's screen is blank
while a death's wait $43 is in the stage setup's part.

Stream.description:
A level marker that sends entities in (Super Mario Bros.' frenzy objects).
Once it appears, and while a slot of the level is free, a new `entity`
comes in `past_edge` pixels past the view's last column, then the next
after `wait` frames plus the next row of the entity's `times` table, in
turn. A shift counter's byte (`draw`, read as a leap's, by the new body's
slot) picks its row of the `heights` table, which is its y; its `ext`
word 0 is that row and word 3 is 1, so a hook sees it is set up. The
marker needs `no_slot`, and it ends once a body of `until` is in the
level. It keeps the wait and the turn in its mechanic words 0 and 1.
Needs a level with `spawn_slots`.

Sway.description: A shuttle's sway across its axis.

Take.description:
What takes an exit: the player's hitbox overlapping `at`, with `hold`
held, and standing if `standing`.

at.description: A box in the level, in pixels.

hold.description: An input action that must be held, such as `down` on a pipe.

if.description:
A counter condition that must also hold, as a transition's `if`:
a door that needs a key.

TileKind.description:
What kind of tile a cell is. The simulation collides by kind: `solid`
stops from every side, `top` only an entity moving down onto its top
row, `ladder` is climbed (and its top stands, for a climber that says
so), `hazard` touches the player as the level's `hazard` says, `water`
and `ice` change falling and running as the level's `water` and `ice`
say. Since core 0.4.6, `coin_block`, `item_block` and `brick` are
solid like `solid`, and a head hit (platformer `jump.head`) tells them
apart: a block with a coin in it, one with an item, a brick. Since core
0.4.16, `coin` stops nothing and a pickup (platformer `jump.pickup`)
takes it.

TilesPicture.description: A picture of tiles, as a sprite lays them out.

palette.description: A palette of the level's palettes (4 to 7 for the sprite ones).

oneOf.description: The player dies: `player.died` fires.

`player.hurt` fires, for the player's state machine to decide what
a hurt does (shrink, or die with `kill-player`).
The player collects it: it's removed and `item.collected` fires.
The player kicks it: `enemy.kicked` fires, for its state machine.

Since 0.4.10: the entity is defeated: it leaves and
`enemy.defeated` fires for it.

Transition.description:
Exactly one of `on` and `after`, or, in an entity's machine, `below`
(with or without `after`).

align.description:
Since core 0.4.12, with `after`: once the time is up, it is taken
only on a frame whose number (the frame count from power-on) is a
multiple of this. Super Mario Bros.' HandleChangeSize steps the
shrink on frames whose FrameCounter is a multiple of 4, so its end
depends on that counter's phase.

align_to.description:
Feature `transition.align_to`, with `after`: once the time is up, it is taken
only on a frame whose counter's first `every` clock has just come
round (its count is 0), so the state lasts to a beat that clock
keeps. Super Mario Bros.' lives screen waits for ScreenTimer, an
interval timer DecTimers counts down once every 21 frames, when
IntervalTimerControl runs out.

below.description:
Feature `transition.below`, in an entity's machine: taken once the entity's
y is at or past this (and its `after` is up, with one). Super Mario
Bros.' PlayerHole ends a death once Player_Y_HighPos reaches 4,
however high Mario was hit.

do.description: Actions to take on the way (docs/model.md lists them).

held.description:
Feature `transition.held`, without `on` or `pressed`: taken on every
frame on which this input action is held, and with `after` only
once that many frames have passed in the state. Donkey Kong's title
sets its idle timer to 64 on each frame Select is held ($C95D).

if.description: A condition that must also hold.

pressed.description:
Feature `transition.pressed`, without `on`: taken on a frame on
which this input action is newly pressed (held, and not on the
frame before), and with `after` only once that many frames have
passed in the state. Donkey Kong's Start pauses the game, and
unpauses it once the pause's 64-frame timer ($0517) has run out.

word.description:
Feature `transition.word`, in an entity's machine with `after`:
taken only on a frame on which one of the entity's mechanic words
is in this range. Donkey Kong's death spin ends on the frame $88
comes round to 4, 120 frames or more after it starts.

Turn.description: Feature `input.turn`: which controller each turn plays from.

actions.description: The actions that read the turn's controller.

counter.description: The counter that says whose turn it is: 0 the first player.

oneOf.description: A pipe or door entered by pressing a direction on it.
A vine or ladder climbed out of the view.
A pipe or door that skips ahead past the next level.
Walking or falling off an edge of the level.

View.description: How the world is seen. Isometric arrives with its projection.

oneOf.description: A side view: down is the direction gravity pulls.

Walk.description:
Walking at a steady speed, turning at walls, and at ledges with
`turn_at_ledges`. It starts facing the player.

bump.description:
Walkers with this turn each other when their hitboxes touch, as
Super Mario Bros.' EnemiesCollision and EnemyTurnAround do.

ledge_at.description:
With `turn_at_ledges`: the ledge is looked for after the move, at
this many pixels across the entity whichever way it faces, in place
of the leading bottom corner before the move, as Super Mario Bros.'
ChkUnderEnemy reads one point under the enemy's middle and
ChkForRedKoopa only reverses the speed.

speed.description: Pixels per frame, without its sign.

turn_after_move.description:
Since 0.4.26: a wall doesn't stop the move. It moves, and if the leading edge of
the tile hitbox's top row is then in a solid tile it turns where it
stands, as Super Mario Bros.' DoEnemySideCheck runs after the move
and only reverses the speed.

walls_at_top.description:
Since 0.4.8: walls are met only at the tile hitbox's top row, as
Super Mario Bros.' DoEnemySideCheck tests two points at y + 20 while
the hitbox reaches the foot at y + 24; a hopper that has sunk into
the ground (`hop.land_first`) doesn't take the ground for a wall.

WalkBump.description:
`walk.bump`: when two walkers test their touch. The test takes each one's
place before this frame's moves, and a pair turns once a touch.

every.description:
A touch is tested on frames where the frame less `phase` is a
multiple of this; 0 never, for a state that leaves the bumping.

view.description:
Only a body with its x this far from the view's left edge, first to
last, takes part, as EnemyOffscrBitsMasked leaves the test.

Walls.description:
Wall points (since 0.4.5), x and y from the entity's position in whole
pixels, tested in order.

left.description: Points on the left side: a wall there pushes the entity right.

right.description: Points on the right side: a wall there pushes the entity left.

When.description: Conditions on an entity's state for a clip. Each one given must hold.

climbing.description: On a ladder or vine (true), or not (false). Since core 0.4.2.

counters.description:
The model's counters are in ranges, each one given, for a picture
the game picks by a timer or a flag the model keeps as a counter
(Donkey Kong's oil drum burns while `drum` is above 0). Presentation
reads the counters; nothing in the simulation reads the clip.
Feature `clip.when_counter`.

ground.description: Standing on something (true) or in the air (false).

invulnerable.description:
In frames where no hurt counts, as after being hurt (true), or not
(false). Since core 0.4.2.

jumped.description:
In the air after a jump (true), or not (false): falling off a ledge
is in the air without a jump. Since core 0.4.2.

moving.description: Moving sideways at all (true) or still (false).

skidding.description: Moving sideways against the way it faces (true), or not (false).

slot_counters.description:
Counters named by the body's slot, each in its range: the test's
`name` followed by the number of the slot the body is in (Donkey
Kong's `barrel_tile` names `barrel_tile0` for the barrel in slot
0), for a picture the game keeps per object slot. A body in no slot
fails it. Presentation only. Feature `clip.when_slot_counter`.

speed_at_least.description: Its sideways speed, either way, is at least this.

word.description:
One of the entity's `ext` hook's words is in a range, such as
Super Mario Bros.' Lakitu ducking into its cloud while its copy of
FrenzyEnemyTimer is below 16. Since core 0.4.21.

words.description:
More word tests, each of which must hold too, for a hook that keeps
what a picture depends on in two words (Donkey Kong's barrels: their
state and their girder). Feature `clip.when_words`.

x_at_least.description:
The entity's x in whole pixels is at least this, for a picture the
game picks by where the object is on the screen (Donkey Kong's
barrel goes behind the oil drum left of x $30, $DFC3). Presentation
only. Feature `clip.when_x`.

x_below.description:
The entity's x in whole pixels is below this. Feature
`clip.when_x`.

WordTest.description: A test on one of a body's `ext` hook words. Presentation only.

at_least.description: The word is at least this.

assets.description: Asset slots by name: what each holds, its role, and where it's filled from.

cost.description:
Feature `cost.frame`: the CPU cycles the original spends on a
frame's work, as terms over the model's state, for a game that steps
its random generator in the time the frame's work leaves
(docs/cycles.md, "The cost model").

counters.description: Numbers the game keeps across levels, such as deaths or score.

evidence.description:
Where each fact comes from, by model path. An entry covers the part
it names and everything under it, unless a more specific entry
covers that.

input.description: Named actions and the buttons that trigger them.

model.description: What the model is and which schema versions it uses.

present.description:
How the game is shown: the screen, the HUD and palette changes over
time. Presentation only: the simulation never reads it.

rules.description: The game's state machines by name, such as playing, dying and won.

stages.description:
Feature `stages`: the original game's stages in the order it plays
them, for a model that holds fewer levels than the game has stages.
